  • Per this reporting, much of the supposed displeasure on Stahl’s part also has to do with Weiss’ perceived lack of experience in the broadcast news industry.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, amid the various changes that have unfolded at 60 Minutes under Bari Weiss’ leadership, a handful of staffers have remained in the fold. Veteran broadcaster Lesley Stahl is one of those people, as she chose to remain with the series alongside cohorts Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim. Up to this point, it seemed that Stahl and Weiss had been able to work together harmoniously. However, if a recent report is to be believed, Stahl is now taking matter with CBS News’ Editor-in-Chief for a major reason.

According to recent reports, this reported situation apparently has to do with editorial autonomy on Stahl’s part. According to the Wall Street Journal (via The New York Post), Stahl is allegedly frustrated with Weiss and co. interfering with her reporting. The news outlet claims that one particular sticking point has to do with changes made to a story involving violence that Palestinians reportedly faced from Israeli settlers in the West Bank. That segment aired back in October after Stahl apparently objected to Charles Forelle, Weiss’ deputy E-I-C, holding it.

Per this reporting, much of the supposed displeasure on Stahl’s part also has to do with Weiss’ perceived lack of experience in the broadcast news industry. Before Skydance (then Paramount Skydance) chief David Ellison hired Weiss in October 2025, she’d founded the online outlet known as The Free Press. That organization was also acquired by Paramount around the same time Weiss was hired. If these claims about Stahl are true, she wouldn’t be the first to question Weiss’ leadership skills.

Another person who has spoken openly about Bari Weiss is former 60 Minutes correspondent, Scott Pelly, who was fired this past May after allegedly accusing the exec of "murdering" the show. Pelley spoke out about Weiss during a subsequent interview and cast doubt upon her ability to run the legacy news brand. It was Pelley’s assertion that the Eye Network was in need of some “adult supervision.”.

Ex-60 Minutes EP On His Biggest Concerns Amid Bari Weiss’ Leadership: ‘That Would Have Freaked Me Out’.

In a recent development, pelley is also one of several former employees who have made claims of “journalistic interference” against the latest leadership team at CBS News. He, Cecilia Vega and more have alleged that they were encouraged to insert what they believed to be news-related bias into their reporting. On the other side of this equation, Weiss and co. have denied presenting biased reporting. Some have also come to Weiss’ defense during this time, with CBS Evening News anchor Tony Dokoupil defending her vision and saying he hadn’t personally seen any instances of bias.

Recent findings suggest that all of that aside, 60 Minutes reportedly finds itself in a tough situation, as the program has seen ratings-related setbacks amid Season 59. One of the latest reports makes note of the show having averaged 8.3 million viewers for its nine episodes that aired between September 9 and November 16. That marked a 16 percent decrease from the previous season. Ahead of that, Weiss addressed concerns about the show and noted it had been doing “tremendously well.”.

If the situation involving Lesley Stahl is legitimate, though, it would mark yet another behind-the-scenes issue for Bari Weiss. Stated conflict would also theoretically add more pressure for Stahl, who’s been receiving backlash for having remained with the show now that Weiss and executive producer EP Nick Bilton are in charge. Time will tell whether any further developments arise in this matter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Literal decades ago, I tried to make a first-person RPG in HyperCard. I got as far as a fateful town gate confrontation before hitting the cap on slides for the shareware version. I mention this because newly introduced, 100% "hand-drawn" first-person dungeon crawler Rise of Furax is uncannily redolent of my long-lost HyperCard game.

This risks being a) a terrible indictment of the game's visual direction, and b) an insinuation that developers Rap2h are dastardly rip-off artists, so let me elaborate that c) I think Rise of Furax looks far, far lovelier than my lousy primordial hypermedia confection and d) it is a legally distinct creation. That unfinished HyperCard concept never left the confines of a Macintosh Performa that is even now rusting on a riverbed. If only I'd pitched it somewhere, I'd probably be a MILLIONAIRE by now. A million pounds is still a lot of money, right? Anyway, here's a teaser video for Rise of Furax.

According to recent reports, the plot setup here is thusly: some apocalypse cult is raising havoc on three islands off the coast of Rivelune. Five heroes – a snake minstrel, a rhino barbarian, a badger knight, a goat sorcerer and… whatever the hell critter that monk is - have been sent to investigate the whole "world is ending" sheebang and do a little levelling.

In a recent development, as in the very first Might and Magic, you steer the party as one, moving around a grid map. Combat is turn-based and there are "secrets, puzzles, and hidden items everywhere". Also schmürpfs. These confuse me even more than the monk character. They look like angry green omelettes. Any pointers? I googled the word and the closest match I could find was Swiss footballer Pascal Schürpf, who appears neither green nor egg-based.

"Every element, from sprites to textures, was hand-drawn on paper," promises the Steam page. It's out April 2027. There's no demo as yet nor even a proper trailer, but god I enjoyed looking at this, in a week otherwise full of screenshots of, like, suggestive scallion distribution in GTA 6. I should finish that HyperCard game. I still remember which river I threw the Performa into.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score.

According to recent reports, while critics have given Rockstar's latest a Metascore of 99, its user score has dropped to 5.6 out of 10 at the time of writing, which Metacritic classifies as "mixed or average". Of the 54,000+ ratings left, 44 percent are "negative".

The score had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.

Some negative reviews raise genuine complaints, such as the game's 30FPS cap on console, while others take issue with how much of the story focuses on Jason and Lucia's relationship instead of the crime-spree antics of past games.

In a recent development, "Expectations might've killed this game," states one 0/10 review. "The hype that something otherworldly would come to be flopped. The hyperrealism makes it feel slow, mundane and boring. Its a tecnichal [sic] advancement for sure but for the wrong reasons. Goodlooks zero personality type stuff. Its not as edgy as the rest of the gta games. And thats exactly my problem like is not funny. The game gets carried by its visuals and radio stations. Certain limitations make it feel like not gta and newly introduced features make it feel like not gta. In the end it feels like a life simulator and the point of gaming is to escape from reality.".

According to recent reports, "Genuinely hated almost every minute of this experience," wrote another. "After years of waiting and an absurd amount of hype, GTA VI somehow managed to leave me more frustrated than entertained. The excessive sexual content gets exhausting, and instead of adding anything meaningful to the experience, it often feels like Rockstar is desperately trying to shock its audience.

It has been revealed that "The story is painfully disappointing, the writing fails to keep me invested, and I honestly couldn't care less about what happens to most of these **** gameplay isn't doing the game any favours either. Glitches, bugs, annoying inconsistencies, and frustrating moments constantly get in the way of actually enjoying the experience. It's ridiculous that a game of this scale, backed by a studio with Rockstar's resources, can feel this rough. I expected a polished experience, not a glorified debugging ****.".

Others point to "woke" and "DEI" agendas.

"A major step down in the writing department compared to previous instalments coupled with the obvious DEI-fication, unfun realism and the resulting player freedom restrictions leave a sour taste in the otherwise detailed gorgeous open world," mentioned one reviewer. Another unhappy player wrote: "Shameful DEI hijacked cuck simulator, the most overrated game of all time and it's not even close.".

According to recent reports, GTA 6 launched on Thursday for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Earlier today, actor Jesse James Rose revealed the game features the series' first non-binary character.

Recent findings suggest that eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Guide: GTA 6: Secret Controls the Game Doesn't Tell You

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (850 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that GTA 6 has a complicated control scheme that allows you to interact with the game in a variety of different ways.
  • Below are 12 secret controls in GTA 6 the game doesn't tell you about.
  • Please note, these all apply to the Default control scheme, which you can enable by pressing Options > Settings > Control Scheme.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GTA 6 has a complicated control scheme that allows you to interact with the game in a variety of different ways. And while Rockstar does a good job introducing almost all of the title's mechanics, several useful features and commands are never mentioned at all. In this GTA 6 guide, we're going to tell you about some of its secret controls.

Below are 12 secret controls in GTA 6 the game doesn't tell you about.

Please note, these all apply to the Default control scheme, which you can enable by pressing Options > Settings > Control Scheme.

Double tap Triangle to get out of your car while the engine's still running:.

This can be useful for when you need to make a swift getaway, as you want waste time needing to start the engine.

One other quick tip here: if you're with a partner and need to quickly get into the back seat, hold Triangle so your character doesn't waste time running around to the passenger side.

If the police know your identity but not necessarily your car, one way you can avoid being detected is by hiding behind the wheel.

Just park up somewhere discreet, and hold Circle to hide from any pursuing police:.

You can rest and lean on any surface by standing close to it and holding the Circle button, like shown:.

This can be useful if you're casing a joint, or just want to watch the world pass you by.

You don't always need words to get your point across. There are situations where a middle finger will do.

Fortunately, GTA 6 has a solution for scenarios just like that.

While on foot, hold L2 and press R1 to give someone the finger:.

You can also do this while driving by simply pressing R1 while behind the wheel:.

Tapping Left and Right while driving will turn on your indicators, allowing you to signal to other motorists which way you're going:.

According to recent reports, this can actually be useful when you're trying to drive safely, as oncoming cars will understand which way you're going and react accordingly. It can also help when you're merging lanes on motorways.

While more complex radio controls can be accessed by holding Left, did you know you can also swiftly turn the radio on and off by double-tapping Left?

This works both in a car and when you're out and about using your earbuds.

If you press Square while driving, you can quickly attack with your car door, as shown:.

This is really useful when you're being flanked by unsuspecting bikers — or you just want to show cyclists who's king the road!

Much like the above car door attack, you can kick any nearby enemies by pushing Square while you're riding a bike, as shown:.

This can help you knock rival motorcylists off their bike, or just give you a good core workout while on the highway.

You can go first-person at any time while you're on-foot and stationary by holding L2 and pressing R3:.

You can move the camera around from this position and press R2 to zoom, but you do need to hold L2 down throughout.

It's also worth noting you can't move while doing this, as there's no traditional first-person mode in the game.

This can be useful for reading signs and other looking closely at other objects in the game, though.

Every vehicle has a full suite of options you can access by holding Left and using the right analogue stick to navigate up to Vehicle, as shown:.

Recent findings suggest that these options can include everything from winding down your windows to turning on your headlights. Speaking of which, you can also toggle your headlights at any time by pressing Circle:.

And, if you're in a boat, you can use the above vehicle management options to set down an anchor, which will keep it in place while you go diving:.

If you're playing on the PS5, the DualSense controller's adaptive triggers will help you observe the speed limit.

While you're driving, holding R2 until you feel the first point of resistance. This is the speed limit.

You'll need to have Adaptive Triggers Resistance enabled to feel this, and you can check it's on by pressing Options > Settings > Controller > DualSense Wireless Controller Features:.

You can take two cars when you're with your partner by using the command menu.

Hold Right to bring up the menu and press Cross/X to instruct your partner to drive:.

Then get in another car and hold Right again then press Square to follow you:.

You'll notice that your partner will drive right behind you, which can be useful if you need to setup getaway cars during robberies:.

Did you know about any or all of these secret controls in GTA 6? You can find even more tips and tricks through the link, as well as tons of collectible and mission walkthroughs in our GTA 6 guide.

James Marsden indicates his comic-accurate Cyclops suit in Avengers: Doomsday gives the audience “everything that they want to see" – even if the actor might not be feeling so snug after stepping out of the black leather.

“The comic-accurate suit was very exciting for me to do, but [they] still haven’t figured out the comfort thing yet,” Marsden told Entertainment Weekly of his brightly colored ensemble piece, which largely mirrors the X-Men leader's traditional wear.

It has been revealed that “No, it was great. It was one of those pinch-me moments where you’re playing this iconic character and then coming back and giving the fans everything that they want to see.”.

Sources indicate that famously, the original X-Men trilogy cracked a joke at the expense of the superhero group's colorful array of costumes. When Hugh Jackman's Wolverine grumbled about the black leather in 2000's X-Men, Cyclops deadpanned if he would prefer "yellow spandex" instead.

Recent findings suggest that in recent years, Marvel Studios has given the X-Men its due on the costume front. Deadpool and Wolverine not only featured Logan in his traditional yellow and blue outfit, but also dealt Gambit a winning hand with his comic book-style suit.

With Disney's acquisition of Fox, Kevin Feige – who had a behind-the-scenes production role on the first X-Men – is finally able to make his cinematic universe dreams come true, with even Marsden admitting there had been "so much chatter" in the past about bringing the mutant team to the MCU.

Industry observers note that so, costume? Check. A fully-fledged role instead of nostalgia bait? Check. A leading light in the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer, complete with iconic catchphrase? Check, check, and check. If you're a Cyclops fan, you'll be eating well this holiday season.

Sources indicate that ho ho ho, the RPS Advent Calendar 2026 is... not ready yet. We haven’t written the words, and I keep forgetting to unblur that new picture of Horace (drawn by the reliably talented Amanda Flagg). But while drag our lumpen feet on the business of deciding our favourite games this year, RPS readers have begun plotting, and scheming, and apparently in some cases, spreadsheeting. That’s right: the Advent Calendar Guessing Game has returned, and is open right now for keen participants.

According to recent reports, if you’re unfamiliar with this grand tradition – which is once again being run by extra-lovely reader Aerothorn on the RPS Discord – then here’s a quick rundown. You, the reader, take a guess at the 24 games we’ve chosen to hide behind Horace’s wall of advent doors this year, finalising your list before the calendar introduces on December 1st. Once all games are revealed, those with the most accurate guesses shall bask forever in the glory of their triumph, and also bag some free access to the RPS Supporter programme. 3rd place wins a three-month subscription, 2nd place wins six months, and the 1st place Guesser Supreme wins a full year of Supp perks.

It has been revealed that be warned, though, that victory will demand a sharp mind and an impeccable memory. Or, at the very least, a willingness to go back through our reviews and What Are We Playing This Weekend posts, to remind yourself which games have taken our fancies these past twelve months. Anecdotally, I think we’ve been slightly better at actually writing about our favourites in 2026 than we were for last year’s calendar, which should hopefully make for an easier Guessing Game. If also, perhaps, a more competitive one?

You can read up on the full game eligibility rules, start discussing your picks, and submit your guesses by joining the #2026-advent-calendar-guessing-game channel in the RPS Discord linked above. Note that you don’t need to correctly guess the position of an included game to earn a point for it, only its presence in the list, though you should specify which game you think will earn the coveted Day 24 door – our overall top game of the year, essentially – as this detail will serve as one of the tiebreakers in the event of a draw.

Sources indicate that thanks again to Aerothorn for setting this up, and good luck to all who participate! Here’s one hint, for free: we didn’t have Sin, Oisin, and Jeremy P voting for the Advent Calendar after having them for the RPS 100, so don’t rely too much on the latter for inspiration. Sorry, Unbeatable.

Recent findings suggest that we know that Pokémon Winds and Waves will launch on Switch 2 at some point in 2027, but that's it. The Pokémon Tech giant is still keeping quiet about the upcoming Gen 10 entry, but an announced gap in the long-running anime has some people already narrowing the release window.

Earlier today, it was revealed that the Pokémon anime would be taking a whopping nine-month gap between the finale of 'Winter Voyage' in December and a new series starring Liko and Roy, which kicks off in October 2027.

According to recent reports, serebii's Joe Merrick was quick to point out that the anime typically doesn't take breaks like this — usually airing an episode a week, bar some minor gaps. Given that fresh series of the show typically launch alongside their mainline game, does this mean that there has been a scheduling change at The Pokémon Company, with Winds and Waves being pushed back until later in the year?

Industry observers note that it certainly seems like a delay behind closed doors is possible — it is strange that TPC would schedule a gap this significant in the anime run intentionally. If the upcoming series is set to tie in with Gen 10, then that would put Winds and Waves launching sometime around October 2027.

Hell, any extra time that TPC can be developing the next mainline title gets a big thumbs up from us.

Of course, it could also just be a wild intended pause in the anime, which had no sway on the game at all. TPC always eyes up the significant pre-holiday November window for its mainline releases, so who's to say Gen 10 would ever have been any different?

Or things could be really off the wall, and this scheduled anime series is actually nothing to do with Winds and Waves, which TPC could go crazy and release any other time in the year instead!

According to recent reports, in short, we're still waiting on something concrete from The Pokémon Manufacturer before we know the next release date for sure. But if this anime start date is anything to go by, we imagine we'll be seeing Gen 10 in the same November window that we're used to.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1157 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's no two ways about it: GTA VI is a blummin' brilliant game, well worthy of its universally acclaimed 99 Metacritic score.
  • Both Fraser and I have put many hours into this enormous RPG already, and have come away floored by its grandeur.
  • We've whipped up a few of our own suggestions and mixed in some from across the world wide webbies to bring you our top improvements we'd like to see in GTA VI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's no two ways about it: GTA VI is a blummin' brilliant game, well worthy of its universally acclaimed 99 Metacritic score. But just because we gave it a 10/10 here at Pure Xbox doesn't mean there isn't still some wiggle room for improvement.

Both Fraser and I have put many hours into this enormous RPG already, and have come away floored by its grandeur. However, we've also noticed a few things we'd like to see fixed or added to GTA VI to make it even better. Think of this article like adding marshmallows to a hot chocolate: we're looking to take something great and make it even sweeter.

We've whipped up a few of our own suggestions and mixed in some from across the world wide webbies to bring you our top improvements we'd like to see in GTA VI. Let's get into it:.

You've all noticed the darkness that appears from time to time around the screen, right? That's a vignette and GTA VI is a big fan of them. It's most noticeable when you're booking it down the North 97 highway or, in the worst-case scenario, flying over the Keys as shown in the above screenshot.

GTA VI uses vignettes to cleverly draw your focus to the most important parts of the screen. I honestly think it's a great technique for making things feel more cinematic. Although, it is quite pants that there's no option to reduce its intensity or turn it off altogether. If Rockstar could give us the ability to toggle the vignette on and off, that would be great, because it also seems to be one of the most requested changes amongst GTA VI players.

Industry observers note that something I've grown increasingly aware of is the inability to wait or sleep to pass time across Leonida. I was particularly irked after an 18-hole crazy golf competition against Jason saw the sun set on us, and I didn't fancy driving all the way back to my lodging in Vice City. I wanted to pass time in my car or a nearby eatery, but my only option appeared to be the 4-5 minute drive home - made worse knowing that once morning hit, I'd just want to do the drive back and play golf in the daylight.

It's probably the fault of Red Dead Redemption 2 and its extremely handy wilderness camps. They were great in a pinch to let you pass time promptly. What would be great is if GTA VI gave players the option to rough it in their car for the night or find a nearby hotel room or something.

I was on a mission to pick up some prescription drugs when my car was escorted slowly into an enemy compound and the camera suddenly switched from third-person to first-person. Seeing Lucia's impeccable nails gripped around the steering wheel made me realise there's no legitimate way to drive from a behind-the-wheel perspective.

Sure, there's that glitch that lets you play GTA VI in first-person, but it would be better if Rockstar implemented an additional first-person POV for driving.

It seems like a bit of a no-brainer, but we'd love to see AMD FSR 4.1 implementation on Xbox Series X. GTA VI is already up-and-running with FSR 4.1 on Xbox Series S which brings internal resolutions up from 720p to 1080p output. It's good going on XSS, but we'd like to see what it can do with XSX.

If a game releases with a good Photo Mode, then you may as well tack an extra 10 hours onto my playthrough. But GTA VI? Maybe add another 20-30 hours. It's gorgeous!

In a recent development, the Photo Mode in this game is already solid. You can set up light sources, adjust focus and aperture, and as a graduate photographer, I think it's all rather intuitive. There's even a selfie mode where players can pose Jason and Lucia together, adjust their facial expressions and change their poses.

What I'd like to see is that same flexibility expand beyond selfie mode. I'd like to be able to adjust the lovers to better match the photos I'm trying to create. It was during a tense getaway, four-stars and neck-deep in trouble, that I thought I'd take an action shot, only to find Jason had blinked and Lucia looked bored as hell. It would be great to have the option to adjust expressions, head directions, poses and all that sort of stuff.

Please fix the sliders when handling amounts of money, Rockstar. Please. It's not the biggest fix, nor the most elaborate, so I'll keep it brief.

Whenever I open my phone to buck myself some cash, I often struggle to select the right amount swiftly. It takes too long for the slider to speed up as I increase the amount, but then it very quickly gets out of control, and I end up overshooting my intended figure. Plus, the sound it makes is quite horrid.

What would help is having set increments to scroll through, say, $1, $10, $50, $100 and so on. It might just smooth out the experience a smidge.

It has been revealed that I'd like to wrap up with a quickfire segment of some of our own suggestions on how Rockstar could improve GTA VI, but also some of yours. So, let's get through it.

I'd love to be able to call NPC buddies like Cal for a round of crazy golf. At the moment, playing with a partner is limited to Jason and Lucia. I'm all for love, but sometimes you need some friendly bonding too.

Another one I'd personally like to see is custom music stations on in-game radios. Now, I know this isn't something likely to happen, but it would be cool to link my Spotify and Rockstar accounts to play my own curated playlists.

In a recent development, oh, and for the love of all things matrimony, please let me make a coffee for Jason/Lucia and actually give it to them. I've experienced Jason asking for a cuppa joe, so let me do the do, y'know?

Industry observers note that something Fraser mentioned he'd like to see is additional minigames like bowling or darts added to the game. The developers said they ran out of time for things like this, so maybe they could add them as a post-launch update.

And to wrap up, I've spotted folks online requesting the ability to dial any phone number like you could in previous games, as well as blind firing around cover during firefights, buying housing property, and having save states pick up directly where you left off.

It has been revealed that so, there you have it. Some of our suggestions and some we've found out in the wild, but we'd love to hear your ideas on what might make GTA VI a better game. Be sure to chat with us in the comments!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This week, amidst ongoing service disruptions, the US Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed that it is "investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems." The bureau, which collects and analyzes transaction data to combat financial crimes, says it has taken some of its e-filing systems offline "as a proactive measure.".

FinCEN hasn't provided an estimate of when the investigation and system disruptions will be resolved, leaving the ability of financial institutions to report suspicious activity and interface with law enforcement indefinitely hampered. Meanwhile, as FinCEN is putting out fires, US Treasury chief information officer Sam Corcos has been busying himself with a different kind of work: He's been vibecoding a Civilization clone.

Corcos' LLM-powered game project was noticed by Bulwark economics editor Catherine Rampell: "The Treasury CIO appears to have spent the past three days vibecoding a Civilization game clone instead of working on this major Treasury database cyber breach," she wrote in a post on X. "As I type this, his Claude code is literally adding theme music.".

A DOGE appointee who previously raised cybersecurity concerns at the IRS with an API "hackathon" and sought to cancel engineering efforts intended to modernize its systems, Corcos is hosting his little LLM project on Github. It's called Legatum, and he describes it as "historical 4X on a hex map, built for people who love Civilization.".

According to recent reports, as Corcos writes in its readme, Legatum is "largely" built with the use of AI coding agents, and all of its art is AI-generated. While FinCEN addresses its cybersecurity breach, Corcos and his Claude agents have been steadily pushing updates: At time of writing, the latest commit—added just six minutes ago—tweaked some of its AI art.

Among the other half-dozen or so commits in the last three hours are adjustments to map generation, music updates, and—let's see—attempts at stemming "a wave of political issues and README vandalism" left by Github customers.

That automated moderation evidently still needs some optimizing, judging from the repo's Problem #220, which reads: "Lead developer is a giant asshole." Another issue notes that "late game American civilization feels broken," because "when you get the Large Language Model tech unlocked, it pretty much destroys any chance of a cultural victory because all your artists are gone, and all your government buildings become totally useless.".

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Industry observers note that finCEN isn't the only US government organization suffering cybersecurity concerns this week. Yesterday, The New York Times reported that the CIA, the Office of the Director of National Security, and the Department of Defense's National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency had been impacted by a vulnerability in an open source intelligence system, which exposed unclassified information.

According to recent reports, on X, Corcos has addressed the questionable optics of overseeing a vibecoded Civ knockoff while his department's facing a cybersecurity intrusion: "Just a heads up, the computers are doing it on their own," Corcos mentioned in a reply to a user who compared the incident to Nero fiddling while Rome burned. "Mostly Opus 5.5 orchestrating a bunch of iterative loops.".

In another reply to a more sympathetic user, Corcos was more enthusiastic: "These tools are getting so good it's blowing my mind. A brief voice note on my phone can kick off an amount of work that would have taken dozens of people weeks to deliver," he said. "So cool.".

Prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a new version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO series, except that it's set during World War 2. I don't believe they had Chryssalids back then. Pretty sure grandpa never mentioned any Chryssalids.

Industry observers note that originally developed by Random Games and published by Strategic Simulations, Inc, the game consists of 18 main scenarios spanning D-Day, Monte Cassino and Cherbourg. There's a mission editor, too, and some standalone extra skirmishes. In each scrap, you pick eight men to undertake such feats as raiding V2 sites and hijacking disabled tanks, drawing on a dizzying range of individual soldier actions. Your squaddies level up with experience, and you can equip them with flamethrowers and bazookas. Among the key differences from X-COM is that there's no morale system - your men will never defy orders. Nor is there an overarching base/Geoscape layer.

In a recent development, "This edition updates Soldiers at War to run smoothly on modern Windows systems, delivering improved compatibility and performance," promises the GOG page (it's also on Steam). "The game now supports 1280x720 widescreen resolution, with rendering improvements for smoother drawing." There are cloud saves and Achievements, too, for today's soldier is not content with merely laying down their life for their country. They must also unlock some percentage-based virtual trophies in the process.

It has been revealed that I remember Strategic Simulations, Inc mostly for working on two games in the Close Combat series, but they developed and published a shedload of other strategy games and wargames before their eventual parent company Ubisoft retired the brand in the noughties. As for Random Games – hold the phone, those guys also made the original Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Phasmophobia's next update, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-fresh piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.
  • The headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School.
  • It has been revealed that the Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Phasmophobia's next update, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-fresh piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.

The headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School. As with the rest of the game's equipment, the higher the Tier, the more accurate the reading, and Tier 3 Dowsing Rods will pinpoint the exact floor the Bone is on.

It has been revealed that the Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from. Icons will show whether a sound is ongoing or a one-off, and you'll be able to use the map to identify ghosts by how fast they move.

It has been revealed that you'll also be able to ask ghosts to interact with doors and switches, and even throw nearby objects, with a list of usable phrases in the Journal. If you're tired of the same maps, you'll be able to build your own pool of maps to randomise from when picking a contract, and upcoming buttons let you swiftly pick small, medium, or large maps.

"We want to ensure every item in our Ghost Hunters' kits can add as much value as possible in investigations," mentioned Daniel Knight, CEO and game director at Kinetic Games.

"Resonance also brings Phasmophobia's move to Unity 6 - while this transition is a technical upgrade first and foremost, it has allowed us to implement major lighting improvements to make the game even more immersive.".

Alongside more realistic lighting and better stability, the switch to Unity 6 also brings expanded graphics and quality options, VR Eye Adaptation, and a suite of colour-blindness settings.

Resonance will also fix several prominent bugs, and introduce a conduct warning system that alerts players before they're banned, except in cases of severe violations.

Phasmophobia is also adding Xbox Play Anywhere support, so if you own the Xbox digital edition, you'll be able to play on Xbox Series X/S, PC, and devices like the ROG Ally.

Resonance is a free update and will be available on all platforms.

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this month, the Phasmophobia community raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it might be hard to believe now, but Bethesda wasn't everyone's top choice for bringing back the Fallout series. In fact, when it came to Fallout 3, Obsidian was the studio many fans wanted to see tackle the wasteland, emboldening the team behind The Elder Scrolls to get things right for the sci-fi RPG.

Recent findings suggest that bruce Nesmith, a long-time developer at Bethesda who worked on Skyrim and the Fallout games (including as a quest designer on Fallout 3), explained the atmosphere back in the mid-to-late 2000s to The Examined Game. "There was huge pushback when Bethesda got the Fallout license to do Fallout 3," he remembers.

"There were a lot of people who were Obsidian fans who were like, 'Bethesda's going to screw it up, they're just going to make it [Oblivion], we want Fallout the way we remember Fallout, these guys should never have had it,'" he notes. "There was a strong vocal community that just hated that we were going to make that game.".

If you can cast your mind back to the era, Obsidian would've seemed like a more appealing choice. Knights of the Old Republic 2: The Sith Lords in 2004 proved the team's ability to handle sprawling science-fiction, and Bethesda's push into open-world design didn't quite blend with the nuance of the early Fallout releases.

According to recent reports, but Todd Howard and his crew weren't about to let the doubters win. If anything, they became more dedicated to making Fallout 3. "We had to prove them wrong," Nesmith says. "And fortunately, we did. And Fallout 3 was embraced, even by a lot of our skeptics.".

He mentions there was a portion of the fanbase who maintain that Fallout 2 was the franchise highlight, and will forever remain so. "But we tried our best to just not engage. You're not going to win that argument, you're not going to persuade hearts and minds," he adds. "All you can do is make the best game you can make and let that be your statement.".

Recent findings suggest that and Fallout 3 is quite the statement. Obsidian did give us Fallout: Newly introduced Vegas in 2010, and then we got Fallout 4 from Bethesda in 2015. When will we see Fallout 5? That's anyone's guess, but Obsidian is apparently working on another game set in the wasteland for the time-being.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The highly anticipated Avengers: Doomsday not only promises sprawling action across the multiverse, but it also features a massive cast (as revealed by that chair promotion last year). However, while the film unites veterans of the Marvel Cinematic Universe and stars who predate it, there are some familiar faces who don’t appear to be in the fold. That includes X-Men veterans Halle Berry and Anna Paquin. I’ve been wondering why they weren’t invited back, and Joe and Anthony Russo shared their takes.

Industry observers note that doomsday features several beloved X-Men stars like Ian McKellen, James Marsden, Rebecca Romijn and the late, great Patrick Stewart (in his final film performance). So, for fans like myself, it’s a bit of a head-scratcher that Berry (who played Ororo Munroe/Storm) and Paquin (Marie D'Ancanto/Rogue) apparently weren’t invited to the party. As part of a cover story for this 2026 movie schedule entry, the Russo Brothers were asked about their absences and those of others, with Joe saying this:.

It has been revealed that [The casting] was really targeted. It was really specific.

Sources indicate that in fairness, the Russos are shrewd when it comes to assembling (no pun intended) the ensembles for their MCU team-up films. Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame both had specific sets of characters that played into the films’ respective narratives in relevant ways. With that being stated, considering the heavy presence of X-Men alums in Doomsday, it’s still somewhat weird that Storm, Rogue, Iceman and more aren’t present when Marsden’s Cyclops states, “To me, my X-Men.” Still, Anthony Russo added another point:.

We really do have a process where we see the entire film through each character’s eyes, no matter what the size of their role is. With the X-Men, we got to really deep dive and think about their histories as characters, their experiences, and how this particular moment in time was gonna affect them. There’s such a rich history to them that we really do bring them to the film as if it’s their movie, as well.

Bringing those OGs into the fold seemed to be the realization of a dream not just for the Russos but for producer Kevin Feige as well. Feige’s producing career notably started years ago when Lauren Shuler Donner tapped him as an associate producer on 2000’s X-Men. Now, the super producer is in the position to have his MCU characters interact with the famous mutants for what may be the latter group’s final stand within the multiverse.

There’s still reason to wonder whether more characters are being kept under wraps ahead of the film’s release. However, earlier this year, when Berry was asked about possibly reprising Storm in Doomsday, she seemed to downplay the idea. The actress does still have plenty of love for the character and the franchise, though, as she celebrated X-Men’s 26th anniversary in July. That post also prompted fans to question her involvement in the upcoming Marvel movie, but nothing has seemingly materialized at this point.

What is known for sure, though, is that a new team of X-Men will be prominent within the MCU moving forward, as a reboot from director Jake Schreier is on the way. With that, new actors will be taking on the lead roles, with Inde Navarrette and Maya Boyd playing Rogue and Storm, respectively. There’s still time for Marvel to surprise us by having Halle Berry, Anna Paquin and others show up in Doomsday but, if not, there’s always Secret Wars.

Avengers: Doomsday opens in theaters on December 18, while Secret Wars is set to follow on December 17, 2027. In the meantime, grab a Disney+ subscription and stream the MCU and X-Men films.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 leaker or leakers Cyberleek claim to to have released the main executable file for an alleged Xbox build of the game that they asserted they'd lobbed onto the net last week. In a fresh statement, the leakers alluded to the excutable being used in attempts to create an unofficial PC port of the crimsim, and denied that their use of cryptocurrency is just a grift.

Referring to the alleged executable as "an early Christmas gift", Cyberleek declared in the statement posted to their website that "the torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects". As of writing, the legitimacy of the executable doesn't appear to have been independently verified, meaning it could still just turn out to be a pile of malware or something similarly dodgy. Needless to say, given that and the fact software piracy is illegal, not touching it - or any of the other files Cyberleek claim to have posted - with a barge pole is the sensible thing to do.

Cyberleek have been bigging up the idea that these files they've been releasing could result in GTA 6 running on PC sharpish, via a modified version cobbled together with generative AI. That might happen, but I'm seriously skeptical that if it were to, it wouldn't just be dodgy jankware than runs like piss, rather than anything that'd compare remotely well to an official PC port.

Thus far, it appears a group of would-be recompilers going by Project Leonida may have got the game to start booting on PC, but they since look to have disappeared and scrubbed their established online presence.

All of this again raises the question of whether the threat of any sort of bodged PC recreation coming out of this alleged executable release may lead Rockstar to narrow the gap between this month's console release and its eventual Windows release, which reports have previously claimed is planned for the opening months of next year.

Recent findings suggest that returning to Cyberleek's latest statement, the leaker or leakers have also taken the opportunity to insist that their attempts to pump up a crypto coin as part of the leaking is just for practical reasons rather than grifty ones, honest. "Every donation is a vote for more of this," they wrote. "Where the votes go, [Cyberleek] follows. Crypto here is just a tool - there is no other way to move funds without names.".

It has been revealed that rockstar called the initial barrage of leaks laid claim to by Cyberleek "heartbreaking". Along with parent company Take-Two, they began a hunt for the identity of the leakers back in August, but that doesn't seem to to have deterred Cyberleek, if indeed the people leaking under the name are still the same ones as in the summer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A rating for the unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has popped up on Korea's Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC).

As Insider Gaming spotted, the board gave Nioh 3 Complete Edition a 19+ rating on 17th November after it was submitted on 2nd November, even though Koei Tecmo hasn't revealed a Complete Edition for the game yet.

The listing, translated by machine, describes it as "a compilation of additional content from the dark Sengoku action RPG Nioh 3", and gives the rating for "excessive expression of violence", noting that "red blood and body amputation frequently occur during combat".

The listing also notes an overseas rating, which Insider Gaming says is a 17+ rating from Japan's CERO.

Unlike some rating boards, GRAC publishes its ratings as soon as they're decided, which is why game listings often surface there before they're officially confirmed.

If Koei Tecmo follows the same pattern as Nioh 2, there may not be long to wait. GRAC's records show Nioh 2 was rated in January 2020, and its Complete Edition followed in November that year. Nioh 3 was rated on 14th November 2025, almost exactly a year ago.

Industry observers note that complete Editions typically includes the base game and all of its DLC. It could even launch alongside Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, which is due in February 2027. Eurogamer has contacted Koei Tecmo for comment and we'll let you know if/when they come back to us.

Back in April, an revision introduced "multiple high-difficulty Battle Scrolls" (side missions), accessible from shrines, the addition of a Stone of Penance item "which increases accessory +Values and rarities in exchange for higher difficulties", and new skills given as rewards for completing the aforementioned high-level Battle Scroll missions.

Eurogamer's review of Nioh 3 called the threequel a new high for the 'masocore' series and "the crucible in which all of Team Ninja's experience has been siphoned into." It's sold over one million copies (and counting) since its 6th February launch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Legendary BBC football commentator John "Motty" Motson, who died in 2023 at age 77, is being added to EA Sports FC 27 through "a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself." The AI-powered recreation of Motson's distinctive voice has the blessing of his family, but some fans of the game are less than enthused.

According to recent reports, motson's history with EA's football series goes back more than 30 years, to FIFA Soccer 96 (which came out in 1995). His last game in that series was FIFA Soccer 2005, according to Mobygames, but he continued to work with EA Sports on the FIFA Manager series. The announcement of his posthumous return to the series claims "almost 10 years of in-game recordings" were used in conjunction with "upcoming AI tools" to put Motson's voice in EA FC 27.

"My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA Sports FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game," John's son Fred stated. "His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole latest set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.".

Fred Motson told the BBC that he believes his father "absolutely" would have wanted his voice to be the game after his death: "I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically—but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects." The BBC report also notes that EA paid the Motson family an undisclosed sum for the right to use John's voice.

According to recent reports, not everyone shares Fred Motson's enthusiasm. While plenty in the EA Sports FC subreddit are excited by the prospect, others refer to it with terms like "shameful," "disrespectful," "gross," and "bloody dark.".

"What a bleak fucking world we live in," redditor forameus2 wrote. "You can't even escape in death.".

"Honestly, it's kind of gross for me," jlo1989 added.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"If anyone from my family uses AI to resurrect me in some perverse way like this, I'll fucking haunt them," niallmul97 wrote.

Peter Caulfield of the Save Our Voices Now campaign against unauthorized voice cloning told the BBC he wouldn't care if Motson had signed a deal with EA allowing it to use his likeness after his death.

"But in life or death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed," Caufield said, adding that family members shouldn't "automatically" have the right to grant permission for AI recreations either.

At least one other game studio has taken a very different approach to the subject: Earlier this year, Darkest Dungeon developer Red Hook Studios said it would never use AI to recreate the voice of beloved narrator Wayne June, who died in 2025, despite having explicit permission from June himself to do so.

"I would never, ever erode his incredible and timeless performances by teaching a machine to sound like him," Red Hook co-founder Chris Bourassa noted at the time.

The Japan Actors Union also recently began a push to protect the rights of voice actors with regard to AI, including a proposed ban on using AI to copy a dead actor's voice unless consent had been obtained prior to their death.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Did anyone really think The Witcher 4 was going to be a PS5 exclusive?

For those who missed it, CDPR confirmed yesterday that it has signed a marketing deal with Sony on its upcoming RPG.

While the details are light, it’s expected this will take the same shape as PlayStation’s arrangement with GTA 6, where the title’s promoted “like” an exclusive – even though it’s technically not.

But it seems there was some confusion online about the nature of Sony’s deal, which CEO Michal Nowakowski has now clarified on social media.

It has been revealed that “We’re looking forward to our partnership with PlayStation! And just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform.”.

It’s as expected really, but Nowakowski still faced follow-up questions about whether Ciri’s story may launch first on PS5, before other platforms.

“All the platforms release at the same time: PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. No one gets left behind.”.

Of course, this is all entirely as expected – the original comments mentioned a marketing deal only, and I don’t think Sony could afford to keep a game as substantial as The Witcher 4 off other platforms, to be brutally honest.

It does hopefully mean the game will be optimised for the PS5, though, taking advantage of unique features like the DualSense et al.

I’m sure we’ll learn a lot more about how Sony and CDPR are collaborating once we get closer to the game’s release.

Industry observers note that following the full game list for Awesome Games Done Quick being released a little while ago, GDQ have now published the full schedule for the event running for a week from January 3rd through January 10th in Atlanta (and streamed on Twitch, of course). Included amongst the fresh games this year are 2026 releases like Queen's Domain, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, the Ocarina of Time remake, and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, which all make a lot of sense as games practically made for speedrunning. Belmont's Curse, specifically, is set to be the event's final bonus game, only to be played if donation incentives are met (which I'm sure they will be, it's a Castlevania game at GDQ).

According to recent reports, but then, there's also Major Walk, which I'm fascinated by the prospect of trying to speedrun as a group. It's listed as a '12 player showcase', which I can only imagine denotes it as more of a fun experiment to put on a show, rather than a world-record aiming speedrun. The chaos of twelve people trying to work together in Big Walk live on the GDQ stage is a spectacle that has my interest, either way. Also making the cut is train-flipping stunt game Denshattack!, which I simply have to mention got a resounding "✨🚂DENSHATTACK MENTIONED🚂✨" from James in the RPS chat this morning. I can't help but share his excitement, in fairness, since Denshattack! is just that cool.

Industry observers note that as for some of the more out-there picks, which I say entirely positively, there's a run of not the DmC reboot, but specifically its bonus Vergil DLC, which is the first time I've heard that mentioned in years. Metroid Prime Origins, a fangame that 'demakes' the famously first-person Metroid Prime into a 2D sidescroller more akin to Zero Mission, is also on the cards; lovely to think there'll be a new speedrun for a new Metroid game just a month before Ravenous comes out. And finally, on a personal note because of my own biases, I'm deeply interested to see the Any% run of Yakuza 5 play out; that game is infamous for its ridiculous scope and length, so watching a runner try to get it down to only its most essential parts should be a treat. The schedule estimates around 2 hours for the run, to which I can only say good luck.

A Grand Theft Auto 6 player says they've been hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network social features ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Posting on Twitter/X on Friday evening, DerrickGott007 remarked they had "just got a 30-day PSN social features ban" for sending the photo, which they'd taken with the in-game camera, through PlayStation's messaging service, warning other players not to do the same.

"Do not, I repeat do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera, across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity," they wrote. "I just got a 30-day PSN social features ban for sending my friend a photo of the nudist colony in GTA6 that I found.".

Recent findings suggest that in a screenshot of the notice, PlayStation Safety states that content sent from the player's account via Message on PlayStation "breached the Code of Conduct", and that their account has been "temporarily suspended from using PlayStation social features for 30 days" due to "pornographic or obscene content". It also warns that "further offenses may result in temporary or permanent suspension from the whole of PlayStation, not just social features".

PlayStation's Code of Conduct asks players not to "share, solicit, access, distribute or store material that is obscene, pornographic or illegal", and says Sony "may take any action as reasonably necessary to protect PlayStation and our players".

Crucially, as Dexerto points out, the code does not make an exception for content taken from games, even ones rated for adults. So if you've snapped anything cheeky in Leonida - say, full-frontal nudity in its nudist resort - you might want to keep it to yourself.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The lack of an official GTA 6 launch on PC hasn't stopped fans from attempting to tackle one themselves, with many projects allegedly making quick progress toward a working version of Rockstar's behemoth – and, now, multiplayer, too.

In case you're out of the loop, this is all being tracked on PortWatch – a platform dedicated to updating folks with progress on every unofficial PC port at the moment in development. As of now, the website claims we're 91.3% of the way to seeing one fully come to fruition… but that's not the most eye-catching news on there. Late last night, PortWatch reported that "GTA 6 multiplayer is running on PC." Yes, multiplayer.

It has been revealed that "TeK's group has players, cars and proximity voice chat working at a stable 25 to 30 fps, on a private fork of CGBJ's build," their update reads. "PortWatch has verified the video is real." For reference, "TeK's group" is one of the teams heading the (again, unofficial) race to get GTA 6 on PC. Apparently, their take on multiplayer features "player characters and vehicles together in the world, with proximity voice chat, so you hear the players near you." It is "private," of course, but still – this is sort of mind-boggling, as PortWatch notes. "Until now, every build we track has been single-player: getting GTA 6's story to run on PC at all has taken everyone's effort. Multiplayer means separate copies of the game agreeing on where every player and car is, and no build on our board had shown that before." Especially seeing as there's been no word from Rockstar on GTA 6 Online.

All of this started with notorious GTA 6 leaker "Cyberleek," who uploaded an executable file for the Xbox build of the game they previously dropped online. That's when groups like TeK picked it up and began working toward a PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6. It's not the only feat fans have taken upon themselves, either. As per VideoCardz, we've seemingly got mods popping up now, too – a possibility that previously felt uncertain thanks to Rockstar's anti-cheat software.

In other words, there's a lot going on right now – but, yet another disclaimer, none of it's official… and it's likely that Rockstar will eventually crack down when things start going live and public (should they do so). Here's hoping we get an actual PC launch someday, though.

Recent findings suggest that we talk a lot about Alexandra Daddario’s style and her knack for hopping on trends like the little black dress and corsets. She’s also been open about her costumes for movies. For example, she’s talked a lot about wearing that iconic red swimsuit for Baywatch. Now, in her newest film, Hershey, she had to wear lots of corsets. When I asked her about that and the stunning period dresses she wore in this film, she told me why they were “fantastic.”.

In the movie about the founding and success of Hershey’s chocolate, Alexandra Daddario plays Milton Hershey’s wife, Catherine “Kitty” Hershey. The film covers a lot of Hershey’s life, from growing up in the late mid to late-1800s to the later years of his life in the mid-1900s. That means it spans the entirety of Milton and Kitty’s relationship. So, for the various decades represented in the project on the 2026 movie schedule, Daddario had different corsets to wear, as she explained:.

It was fantastic, and it was interesting to see. You know, they were like historians in costumes. And I didn't realize that there were different kinds of corsets for different decades, different time periods, I should say. So we had different corsets as Kitty gets older, and that was interesting and helped me get into character.

Industry observers note that I can totally see how the corsets helped Daddario. While painful at times, they alter how you carry yourself. So, I’d imagine that having different ones for different times in her character's life helped her figure out how to stand, move around and evolve Kitty’s physicality.

Milton and Kitty were married from 1898 to 1915, when Kitty died. So, in Hershey we get to see their meet-cute, and Daddario wearing a gorgeous pink corseted dress and floral hat. We also see their final days together. It’s an emotional tale, and as their relationship evolves, so does Kitty’s fashion (and corsets).

In a recent development, now, when I asked The White Lotus actress about her favorite outfit, she stated she couldn’t pick a specific one. However, she did call out another element of her costumes that helped her get into character:.

It has been revealed that they were all so beautiful and great. I love the hats; they were just so out there. And she, Kitty, wore these incredible hats. So that really helped me get into character and have some fun.

Industry observers note that I love how much these looks helped her get into character. As someone who has been a fan of Alexandra Daddario’s fashion game for years, I was looking forward to speaking with her about her outfits in Hershey, because they stand out so much. They’re beautiful and fitting for the time, and I think it’s so cool that they really helped the actress find her character.

Now, if you’d like to see Alexandra Daddario as Kitty, you can catch Hershey in theaters now.

Industry observers note that despite being revealed back in 2022 with an initial release window of 2025, NEKCOM's action RPG Showa American Story has been set for a late 2026 release date for a while now. That seems to have changed, however, as the release date on its Steam page has slipped to 2027 without any sort of announcement as to why.

In conversation with Automaton last month, the game's director Xiangyu Luo stated that "The game's content is already completely finished, and we're now at the stage of polishing its overall quality." As such, it would seem that this delay is to give the game a little more breathing room for bug fixes and quality assurance work, rather than rushing a holiday release just to hit its stated release window.

Based on my own time with Showa American Story, taking a little more time to clean it up would be a welcome choice. When I played a demo at Gamescom 2026, I was a little stunned by how awful it felt to play. The protagonist was a blank slate designed to be pretty and nothing more, and the combat was mind-numbingly oversimplified, its challenge mainly derived from the need to wrestle with its janky controls and the noticeable delay between button presses and attacks. In that same interview, Luo notes an awareness of the game being compared to the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series in being a 'wacky' open-world action RPG, saying that he's "happy that players are making that association", as "it means they've recognised Showa American Story as a rich RPG with plenty of content to sink their teeth into." I can respect him taking the comparison in stride, but what I played seemed like a pale imitation of LAD that missed what makes that series more than it seems on the surface.

I can hope that this delay can result in improvements to the critiques the game has faced — Luo did mention that "we've heard many valuable comments regarding the feel of the controls and how the action is presented" — and that Showa American Story releases in a good state sometime in 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, paying for access to online multiplayer has been the norm on Xbox consoles for decades now. It's something we've come to expect as part of playing online with friends and other folk around the world. The general understanding is, if you don't have Xbox Live, you're not playing online.

Eight years ago, I bought a gaming laptop to play Battlefield V on the go, and ever since paying for access to online multiplayer hasn't made much sense to me. It's just not something you do on PC. Sure, games like World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy XIV require additional subscriptions in order to play, but the majority of online games, like BFV, only require you to upfront the retail cost and crack on.

Xbox Play Anywhere is probably where console paywalls really start to look silly. Just a few months ago, I bought Subnautica 2 to play with a friend through the Xbox PC app. I could've opted for Steam, but I wanted to work towards those Xbox cheevos (when they eventually arrive). For a couple of weeks, I'd hop on the PC and dive into alien waters with my mate.

One day, I fancied playing on the big screen in my living room, so I installed Subnautica 2 on my Xbox Series X, booted it up and was prompted to buy a Game Pass subscription just to play the same save file I'd been enjoying for weeks through the Xbox PC app. Like I mentioned, a bit silly.

Time went on, and I'd more or less let this go from my head until I read a report from Windows Central a couple days ago, claiming that Microsoft's upcoming Xbox Helix next-gen console could have aims to kill paywalls for paid multiplayer.

"Sources close to Microsoft's intends tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer.".

In a recent development, according to Jez Corden, the original plan for Xbox Helix was to create a console-PC hybrid with access to Steam, potentially spelling the end of Xbox's staple multiplayer charges. It kind of makes sense when you think about it. If you can play your Xbox games across both console and PC, whether through disc-to-digital or Xbox Play Anywhere, it seems like pointless friction to lock multiplayer behind a paywall depending on which device you're playing on.

Recent findings suggest that back in 2021, changes to Xbox's paid multiplayer requirements allowed players without an active Xbox Live Gold subscription to access multiplayer free-to-play titles such as Fortnite, Call of Duty: Warzone and Apex Legends. And today, Xbox Live Gold isn't even a thing, as it's been absorbed into Xbox Game Pass.

So, even if Xbox Helix's original vision has changed somewhat from what Corden initially reported, it's still not out of the question to suggest that paid multiplayer could eventually become redundant.

In a recent development, pure Xbox, we'd love to hear what you think about this. Make sure to vote in the poll below and tell us more in the comments section.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day, more than half of everyone playing on PS5 and Xbox was playing GTA 6.

Citing new data from Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, analyst Mat Piscatella said on Bluesky that 61 percent of US PlayStation 5 players and 56 percent of global Xbox players who were active on 19th November "engaged with Grand Theft Auto 6".

PS5 players averaged 513 minutes in GTA 6 that day, which is over eight and a half hours, while Xbox players averaged 494 minutes, or around eight and a quarter hours.

"Both the DAU [daily active users] and minutes played engagement rates are absolutely bonkers," Piscatella wrote.

For comparison, Fortnite had the second-highest engagement rate that day, with 10 percent of active players across both platforms playing it.

Piscatella also shared the top five games that GTA 6 players had been playing in the two weeks before launch, between 6th and 19th November: Fortnite, Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto 5 (Remastered), Roblox, and NBA 2K27.

According to Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, Grand Theft Auto VI had a massive launch (surprise!).For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto VI.PS5 GTA VI players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494.

The figures come after Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 had become the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's one of the best-reviewed games of all time, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

GTA 6 vault: How to open them during big bank jobs

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission, you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.
  • Here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opening a GTA 6 bank vault is one of the best ways to make off with a significant score during a robbery, with potentially $100,000 or more in bills and valuables from a single heist.

But those huge bank vault doors are completely impenetrable, and confusingly, even after you've learned how to drill into a vault as part of a Chapter 3 story mission, you still won't be able to open vault doors in open world bank robberies.

Here's the trick: you've got to get someone to open bank vault doors for you. Only then can you steal all that sweet cash.

Your GTA 6 fence, Yasmani, will begin offering you tips once you start selling him stolen goods in Chapter 3: jewelry store heists targeting specific items and which ATM jobs have the most cash, for example. These are worth doing anyway as they get you the snap gun.

Sources indicate that complete every job Yasmani has and keep asking for more, and in Chapter 4 he'll offer you a tip for $10,000. Pay it, and he'll give you the locations of two security vans (armored cars) in Vice City. They'll show up on your map as pink icons.

It has been revealed that there are multiple banks with vaults that armored cars visit. While driving around the areas near these banks and keeping your eyes peeled, you may spot an armored car without Yasmani's tip. It could take quite a while, though!

You can see which banks have vaults by looking under "Massive Bank Jobs" in the "Robberies" category on your map. There are four big banks in Ocean Beach, two downtown, one in Tequesta, and one at Vice City International Airport.

Follow the armored car until it parks outside a bank. Watch as one of the drivers gets out and walks into the bank. You can follow him to see where he goes, though bank layouts differ and he may take different routes. He may walk through the front doors, or he may go in a side entrance or a roll-up door in the back.

Once he's all the way inside—not just inside the front doors, but deep into the bank—he'll head to the vault and open it.

It has been revealed that you can't open that vault yourself! Only the armored car driver can. That's the trick.

It has been revealed that once the guard is in the back of the bank, begin the robbery. Search for the vault in the back. You may need to use explosives to open the door the guard went through, or you can look for a door you can open with the snap gun. You'll find the vault door open with the armored car driver nearby. Subdue him and grab all the cash off the cart inside the vault.

It has been revealed that there are several safe deposit boxes in the vault you can open for extra loot. Use your focus ability to highlight which boxes you can loot, and shoot them to open them up. You can also blow open all the boxes at once using a grenade or sticky bomb. Grab the loot from each.

If you really want to clean the place out, there's still all the cash drawers in the front of the bank and a small safe, or multiple safes, somewhere else, usually in an office in the back. You can open these standard safes with safe codes.

The armored car parked outside has loot in it, too. The thing is, it may despawn while you're inside the bank. If you want to loot it, place a sticky explosive on the rear door, which won't let the truck despawn. (Be stealthy: there's another guard still watching the truck). When you leave the bank after the robbery, detonate the bomb and grab the loot.

Sources indicate that the best way to enter a bank is through a back door, if the building has one, (using the snap gun to avoid alarms) or a roll-up door. If the guard you're following goes in the back, he may leave the doors unlocked behind him, and you may not even have to unlock any doors at all to reach the vault. Just be prepared to run into multiple security guards and employees you'll need to subdue.

Sources indicate that you will want both Jason and Lucia along for any bank vault jobs you pull. There is so much cash and valuables to grab you'll easily fill up four bags, which requires two people to carry. (You can hand loot bags to your partner by interacting with them and choosing the "Hand over bag" prompt). You'll also want one character to work as crowd control while you're looting the bank.

A silenced gun is a good idea: you want to delay setting off alarms for as long as possible, and if bank employees or citizens hear gunshots they may panic and trigger the alarm, or flee from the bank and call the cops.

In a lot of robberies you can find the security footage and destroy it while the robbery is in progress. Big banks have cloud-based cameras which won't allow you to destroy the footage. Keep a lookout (using focus) for cameras and shoot them out (with silenced pistols) as quickly as you can.

Recent findings suggest that if an alarm goes off during a vault robbery, you'll get an instant four-star wanted level, which means SWAT trucks, roadblocks, and helicopters. Park your car in a good spot outside so you can jump into it easily, and have some idea of where you want to drive to during your escape.

In a recent development, dancing Dragons Games and Hooded Horse have confirmed Symphony of War II: Dominion, the sequel to 2022's Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga. Sin noted the original as pretty special for being "a good strategy game", highlighting the unique importance of taking care of each and every army member, rather than just benching the ones that are less effective and/or pretty to look at. The Nephilism Saga is also somewhat rare in being a turn-based tactics game made in RPG Maker, as seems to be the case with its sequel, which is expanding to include naval combat.

Symphony of War II: Dominion Announcement Trailer | Strategy RPG Watch on YouTube.

Dominion's premise mirrors its predecessor in setting a band of heroes from a wide variety of classes, with units ranging from heavy knights and light archers to cannon-lighting artillery and even dragons the size of large dogs; I do have to wonder if an actual hooded horse is one of the units. Over 100 different classes are available, with the core of the game being swapping out these units to create the most effective squads of units for each turn-based battle. As before, it's not just a matter of recruiting soldiers and never thinking about them again until their turn arrives; a cared for army is a strong army (Sun Tzu stated that, probably), and nurturing your army with new gear, individual perks and specialisation to make the squad work not only on their own, but as a collective.

Phil Hamilton, founder of Dancing Dragon Games, elaborated that "With Symphony of War: Dominion, we’re building on what players loved about the first game while taking the series in a direction we’ve wanted to explore for years. We’re delivering a deeper, more ambitious strategy RPG without sacrificing the feel and flow that made the original special." Symphony of War II: Dominion releases sometime next year, so for now, get thinking about how you'll best take care of your squads. To paraphrase Sun Tzu again, keeping them fed is always a good start.
