It has been revealed that the beauty of stepping into a digital world is that it allows me to accomplish things I couldn't possibly dream of doing in the real one, like, say, climbing anything that's higher than your average step ladder. White Knuckle is one such game that's all about playing around with uncomfortable heights, and a new patch for the early access roguelike went live this week introducing a new, hostile environment: The Core.

According to recent reports, the sixth region to be added to the game, and the "penultimate challenge," implying that there's just one more area to come after this one, The Core takes you to Habitation Blue's reactor sector. "Use everything you have available to fight through the now Mass-controlled Superstructure Automated Processing System (SAPS) and her array of mechanized defenses," explains a Steam news post. "The Core is the sterile power station of the Superstructure, a massive network of coolant lines, offices, catwalks, and more, all of which is highly secured by an army of turrets, drones, and androids. Even without the Mass hot on your tail it would not be easy to escape.".

There are a few new subregions to be found too, of course, but more importantly a new major artifact. It's called The Scissors, and with it you cut off your hands ("yes, really") to "gain a spectral form that increases your reach, hand stamina, and damage," while using the artifact. You can also throw the scissors like a boomerang to hurt enemies from afar, and "killing enemies also counts as eating if using Survival Mode binding, or the perks Conditioned Polyphagia & Unstoppable Conviction.".

According to recent reports, beyond this there's a selection of upcoming weapons, like the piton crossbow which shoots "pitons at range, to set up routes and to deal extreme damage." The pulse pump is a new trinket that introduces a chargeable mid-air jump. There's new perks like one called nest egg, where you gain a "second major artifact at the start of the Nest, at the cost of halving all roach deposits in your run." Previous regions have also received some new room tiles, and there's a few fresh cosmetics to pick up too. There's some secret thing to find in this patch as well, "but you'll need to play to find out…" Hop to it, I guess!

Doctor Strange 2 explores the multiverse, but its Doomsday legacy is proving Marvel can fix mistakes

💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the road to Avengers: Doomsday, the multiverse is a touch too familiar.
  • So, who better than the Sorcerer Supreme to tap into the magic of that concept alongside a handful of genius what-if castings and a deliciously evil villain in Scarlet Witch?
  • According to recent reports, but even before cameras began rolling, there was an obvious issue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the road to Avengers: Doomsday, the multiverse is a touch too familiar. But back in 2022, our expectations were limitless as the walls broke down between several cinematic universes amid Disney's acquisition of Fox.

So, who better than the Sorcerer Supreme to tap into the magic of that concept alongside a handful of genius what-if castings and a deliciously evil villain in Scarlet Witch?

According to recent reports, but even before cameras began rolling, there was an obvious issue. A movie called Multiverse of Madness has to live up to the promise of its title. The Doctor Strange sequel certainly delivered on that potential from the outset by installing Evil Dead and Spider-Man's Sam Raimi as director. Already, Marvel had a winning hand – and Raimi made it count. After Loki and Spider-Man: No Way Home cracked open the door to alternate worlds inside the MCU, Doctor Strange 2 swept across planets and fired through different realities – ensuring a comic book movie played out, well, actually like a comic book for once. Groundbreaking, I know.

This being Sam Raimi, though, there's a playful mix of horror and heartache alongside the trippy visuals. Scarlet Witch may be the focus, but Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness was propelled along by Stephen Strange's reluctance to let Rachel McAdams' Christine Palmer, the love of his life, go for good. This isn't Peter Parker and MJ's will they/won't they romance, but a more mature way for a hero to realize he doesn't always get the girl and hits harder than I expected upon a rewatch.

On top of the emotion, there was a generous helping of fan service, largely thanks to Earth-838's Illuminati.

Patrick Stewart once again taking a seat as Professor Xavier feels especially welcome in the weeks since the actor's passing, while the rest of the group tasked with staving off multiversal threats – Captain Carter, Black Bolt, Lashana Lynch's Captain Marvel, Baron Mordo, and John Krasinski's Mister Fantastic – were a grab bag of fancasting favorites and second chances that harnessed the creative brilliance of the multiverse.

Industry observers note that welcome to Road to Doomsday, GamesRadar+'s weekly MCU rewatch series. Over 15 weeks, we'll be revisiting each Marvel movie and TV show on Disney's list of essential movies to watch ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, sharing our thoughts upon rewatching and deciphering what we can learn about the next Marvel mega-event from each entry. Why not relive some MCU highlights and watch along with us?

In a recent development, elsewhere, Scarlet Witch is a strange case – no pun intended – in Multiverse of Madness. Elizabeth Olsen openly admitted to being the only real authority to the movie's creatives about how her character arc went in WandaVision (she finished filming the Disney Plus series just days prior to production beginning on the Doctor Strange sequel). While the hunt for her children across realities made sense in theory, it becomes too huge of a leap for someone who was at least coming to terms with her losses by the end of her time in Westview.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

It all culminated in a death that was dramatically heavy, but left her family – and the audience – with too many loose ends and a gnawing sense of loss across Agatha All Along and VisionQuest.

It has been revealed that but dead doesn't always mean dead in comic book movies. In the grand scheme of the MCU, Scarlet Witch's demise was keenly felt, even if we collectively knew it wasn't necessarily permanent.

The decision to retcon her inevitable revival into a way to entrench Doctor Doom's position as the next Big Bad of the multiverse was an inspired one.

Industry observers note that enter Doctor Doom. In the VisionQuest post-credits scene, Robert Downey Jr.'s masked supervillain arrives at the ruins of the Darkhold Castle in Mount Wundagore to resurrect Wanda and claim her powers for his own twisted quest to save the multiverse. In one fell swoop, it makes the end of Multiverse of Madness and what comes next in Avengers: Doomsday all the more interesting – not least because we know just how powerful Scarlet Witch is in the MCU. Doom already has Hulk and Scarlet Witch on his side, with Spider-Man possibly on his radar too. Turning some of Marvel's most iconic heroes against the Avengers (via fair means or foul) would open up far more narrative possibilities than an all-against-Doom battle.

Avengers: Doomsday sounds like the darkest Marvel movie yet, which is why it needs a pinch of Deadpool & Wolverine.

Then, there are the incursions. Admittedly, Doctor Strange and the Multiverse of Madness' post-credits scene isn't all that memorable. Not yet, anyway. Charlize Theron's Clea showing up to tell Doctor Strange he needs to clean up some cosmic mess, though, at least allows Marvel Studios to retroactively act like incursions were present throughout the past half-decade's stories. The literal collision of universes is a major deal, with the Russos even describing it as a "profound" devastating event. Much like Scarlet Witch's arc and return, it's a neat piece of tidying-up for something that otherwise rang hollow.

It has been revealed that as the joke goes, Kevin Feige can look you dead in the eye and tell you something was always the strategy, despite overwhelming evidence to the contrary. That has never been more obvious – and better implemented – than in the connective tissue between Multiverse of Madness and Avengers: Doomsday.

Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness is available to stream now on Disney Plus, ahead of the release of Avengers: Doomsday on December 18 in the US and 16 in the UK.

It has been revealed that look ahead with our list of upcoming Marvel movies and check out how to watch the Marvel movies in order ahead of your next rewatch. See you next week as we revisit Thunderbolts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Dawn of War 4's December release date inches ever closer, a newly introduced trailer appears to have teased a fan-favourite character's inclusion in the RTS's first post-launch DLC.

It has been revealed that the trailer, which covers the Commander Edition of Dawn of War 4, includes a breakdown of all the extra stuff packed in alongside this version of the game. This includes the digital soundtrack, three-days of early-access to the game, and the story prologue. It'll also include the Aftermath post-launch DLC too, with its dedicated campaign and fresh playable faction.

Industry observers note that now, ever since the Aftermath DLC was revealed, people have speculated it would be chaos-focused. The design of the DLC logo is black with a gold trim, an often-used colour scheme for the faction. However, which sort of Chaos was left up to debate. That is, until this trailer, where the answer is seemingly given away with a cheeky tease.

In a recent development, in its final few seconds, the trailer indicates a pair of glowing yellow mechanical eyes peering out from a gloomy background. This was swiftly identified as almost-certainly Vashtorr the Arkifane, a relatively new addition to Warhammer 40,000 and a fan-favourite baddie all around.

Industry observers note that vashtorr as a character has been getting a lot of love ever since his introduction in 2023. It was then, during the Arks of Omen campaign for the tabletop game, that he played a central part in the narrative event bridging the game's 10th and 11th edition. Since then he was the main antagonist of Boltgun 2, and was central in the 2025 novel Achmagos.

What this means for Dawn of War 4 is that, if he is a commander of Chaos forces, expect a lot of machinery and demon engines on his side. That's kind of his whole deal. Whether that means he's paired with tech-focused Dark Mechanicum as a sort of mirror to the Adeptus Mechanicus faction already in the game, or if he'll come alongside Chaos Space Marines to better reflect the Dark Angels / Blood Ravens remains to be seen. It could also be a mix of both! We'll have to wait and see.

There can be such a wonderful charm that comes from fan games because the people that make them really are just in it for the love of the (literal) game. They ain't gonna make any money from this thing! So I'm quite tickled by OpenZ, a 3D remake of the 1996 RTS game Z from The Bitmap Brothers that's completely open source (and, thankfully, hand made).

At the moment there's only two levels, though it's sounding like it's the full run of them, described as having been "meticulously restored and polished to an extreme level of detail," with some added improvements thanks to "30 years of RTS game design experience." There's a few newly introduced bits to find in this remake too, like new mech and electrobot units.

It sounds like there are bigger prepares for the remake overall, presumably for the full game too: "This is only the beginning. Together as a community we can bring Z back to its former glory: more restored classic levels, completely original latest levels, new units and maybe even multiplayer." As mentioned, it's completely free to download and play too, so where's the harm in giving it a go!

GTA 6 has weird purple streetlights because actual Florida screwed up its streetlights

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (596 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When you're exploring a world as realistic and well-observed as GTA 6's Leonida, it's rare for a piece of benign infrastructure to stick out.
  • Maybe, but it's awfully specific, and I had a feeling there was a deeper intention behind it.
  • So Henry reached out to friends in south Florida, the region that Leonida's biggest cities are based on, and they cracked the case wide open.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When you're exploring a world as realistic and well-observed as GTA 6's Leonida, it's rare for a piece of benign infrastructure to stick out. But on night one of my playthrough, I clocked some weird streetlights.

Why are some of them turquoise?

A stylistic choice by Rockstar? Maybe, but it's awfully specific, and I had a feeling there was a deeper intention behind it. So I DMed my buddy Henry, an honest-to-god Floridian who was also playing GTA 6, and asked what's up. At first he thought strange streetlights in the Key Lento area of the map were special lights meant to not disorient turtles, but those are typically red, so probably not. And that doesn't explain the purple ones.

So Henry reached out to friends in south Florida, the region that Leonida's biggest cities are based on, and they cracked the case wide open.

"The purple [lights] are definitely real. We have a ton of them down here because whoever is in charge of that in the government bought a bunch of defective lights," the anonymous Floridian responded.

Yes, actual Florida cities are lit by these dubiously dim, yet undeniably cool purple lamps. According to ClickOrlando, residents first started reporting the purple streetlights in 2023. They put up hundreds of these things across the state before they started malfunctioning—it was such a kerfuffle that the government eventually released a statement saying their vendor really screwed the pooch.

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It has been revealed that apparently the cause was a "spectral shift caused by phosphor displacement," which essentially means the LED lights were always blue, but the coating that was supposed to make appear yellow or white or whatever didn't work. The powers that be mentioned the malfunctioning lights would be replaced, but judging by our own sources in the state, they haven't gotten them all.

So that's fun. If you already heard about this somewhere (other than your Floridian friend), it's probably because YouTuber AnyAustin also clocked these lights in his video published yesterday. Glad I'm not the only one who couldn't resist this rabbit hole.

Industry observers note that I like how Rockstar didn't go overboard with these lights—just like the genuine article, they're in and around parts of Leonida, but not everywhere. I'm still not sure how to explain the turquoise ones, though. A lot of local news, Reddit, and YouTube skimming did not produce a clear answer, other than other cities in America that do have green streetlights sometimes. Perhaps Key Lento has lamps busted in a slightly different way, or it's just a calming shade of blue that Rockstar thought looked nice. It does, to be fair.

We've got some new data coming out about the UK games market in November 2026 today, and unsurprisingly, it's a market that's been absolutely dominated by the launch of GTA 6 last week.

According to the folks at The Game Business, sales of the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S rose by a whopping 75% during GTA 6's launch week, which represents the biggest jump for Xbox hardware since 2024.

The PS5 was close behind at 46%, and console sales were up 38% overall (after a 29% increase the week before).

In terms of UK console sales, PS5 sales rose 46% during the week GTA 6 came out, while Xbox Series S and X sales jumped 75%. It’s the biggest jump for Xbox since 2024. Overall, UK console sales last week were up 38%, which comes on the back of a 29% increase the week prior.

Meanwhile, the controversial "physical" edition of GTA 6 broke numerous records in Europe, serving as the biggest physical launch in Spain's history according to their charts, and selling over 1m physical copies in France in three days.

Recent findings suggest that it was also the biggest physical launch in the UK since FIFA 20 in September 2019, and is the 17th biggest physical launch since records began there in 1995. This is according to data provided by UK data tracker Nielsen IQ.

It has been revealed that "GTA 6 is the biggest physical game launch since 2019, reveals UK data tracker Nielsen IQ. It generated £32 million in revenue in just three days.".

It has been revealed that just last week, on the day of GTA 6's release, we mentioned how Xbox hardware spending in the U.S. was up 42% YoY in October, attributed to the likes of Gears of War: E-Day and GTA 6.

It's going to be fascinating to see how the rest of the world stacks up in terms of Xbox sales data from November (which should be revealed over the coming days and weeks), and indeed whether GTA 6's physical edition is also setting records in even more regions. It most likely is - this is a ridiculously popular game after all.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At this point, it’s well known that Switch 2 is by far the market leader in Japan.

While the PS5 still commands some marketshare, it gets dominated by the Nintendo machine on a weekly basis.

GTA 6’s launch is significant, then, because for the first time in a while it’s pushed Sony’s console in front of the Switch 2 – albeit only by a few thousand units.

According to Famitsu’s latest report, the PS5 sold 41,472 units through the week ending 22nd November, while the Switch 2 managed 36,817 units.

In a recent development, this is an incredibly rare scenario, and likely won’t be repeated again (if ever). But it indicates that with the right software, Sony can put up a fight domestically against Nintendo.

The organization’s been taking the region a lot more seriously under Japanese CEO Hideaki Nishino, launching more affordable region locked units to try and stimulate interest.

This week saw the release of the upcoming Midnight Black model, which certainly helped contribute to the sales.

But PS5’s success was primarily motivated by GTA 6, which sold a very respectable 200,759 units at retail for the week.

That’s slightly less than GTA 5’s 304,752 units opening in 2013, although remember digital buying habits have changed dramatically in the last 13 years, and GTA 6’s physical release was not particularly compelling as it doesn’t include a disc.

A good week for Sony in its home region, then – one that’s unlikely to be replicated, but should be taken as a sign it can compete with the right lineup and pricing model.

[source famitsu.com, via gematsu.com].

There are many different kinds of smarts, and the kind of smarts I am are absolutely zero help when it comes to games like Astario, a spaceship and space station building factory sim reminiscent of Factorio that just introduced into early access. I think there's just so many moving parts in ways I can't wrap my head around, but I'm fairly confident that some of you will be, so I'll try to use the smarts I do have to tell you about it a bit more.

Astario puts you in a spaceship in, uh, space, and oh what a major space it is. I have no idea if it's a to scale universe or anything, but it certainly looks quite expansive. There is a Minecraftian quality to it in that you must fly about and find resources from things like asteroids and other bits of technological scrap, all of which is divided up into blocks. You can get quite granular with it, inspecting each individual cube up close to see if it's a material that you can make use of, adding it to your haul for use elsewhere.

As you acquire different kinds of blocks, be they functional or structural, you can build up various upcoming vehicles and "create an imposing machine where all components work together to achieve your goal. Plan or design your build out of armor blocks, power supplies, life support components, tools, and production machinery. Construct an orbital station with a stash of cargo containers, or anchor your production base to an asteroid and turn its ores into more blocks, fully automatically. Equip your ship with docking ports for refueling or recharging." How you build things is up to you, you've seemingly got a lot of free reign in terms of artistic expression.

And then of course there's bits of production machinery you can produce that in turn net you recipes and the like so you can continue to improve your ship or space stations. "All production blocks have input and output ports that can be automated using logistic pipes which use request-based item routing," explains the game's Steam page of how techy you can get with it. "Simply hook up your inputs to a cargo container, and the machine will pull what it needs. Mining can be temporarily automated using specialized drills, which mine until the resources within its scope are depleted." If any of this sounds like it's up your alley, then you can pick up Astario on Steam in early access now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Banjo-Kazooie - the iconic Rare platformer starring an absent-minded bear and the sassy red bird he carries in a backpack - has been on hiatus for years, but a new Activision job listing has raised hopes for a new game.

In a LinkedIn post advertising a 'Product Manager, Emergent Franchises' role, the publisher wrote that it's "home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, and now… Halo, Age of Empires, Sea of Thieves, and Banjo Kazooie.".

In a recent development, "Become part of the team working on building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises," the listing goes on. "As a Product Manager, you will serve as the publishing product lead for an upcoming premium console & PC title, driving the product from concept to launch.".

Recent findings suggest that if you're scratching your brain trying to remember when Activision took control of the beloved platformer, well, it happened during Xbox's last massive internal shakeup. Amid the mass layoffs and studio divestments, Xbox also made some drastic changes to its corporate structure - Halo, World's Edge and Rare were all slotted under Activision's supervision.

Rare's 40-year history includes almost too many notable games to list, but the internal rejig presumably put Activision in control of games like Conker, Viva Pinata and Killer Instinct, alongside the aforementioned pirate hit Sea of Thieves and Banjo-Kazooie.

The job post is by no means confirmation that a upcoming Banjo-Kazooie game is in development, but it is the only series named here that can be considered dormant, perhaps hinting that Activision has plans to revive it down the line. Crash Bandicoot 4 and Spyro: A Realm Beyond lay out a pretty good blueprint for its return, I think.

The last properly new game in the series came 18 years ago with the Xbox 360's Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts, a surprisingly good physics-driven vehicle construction sandbox.

Since then, Banjo and Kazooie revealed up as a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros Ultimate. More recently, a fan-made PC port and an Evercade Double Pack have kept the series chugging.

In a recent development, composer Grant Kirkhope was slightly more hopeful about the prospect of a Banjo-Threeie back in September. "I do know of like three companies that have actually physically pitched to Microsoft or to Rare about making another Banjo-Kazooie game, and I don't think anyone was successful," he remarked at the time.

Netflix's The Body was one of the unexpected hits of the 2026 TV schedule. While it's still yet to be confirmed whether we'll get to stream a second season with a Netflix subscription, it feels like the odds are looking good. So I'm glad the executive producers/showrunners are already shooting down some fan theories before any fresh episodes come out.

In a recent development, unfortunately, creator Quinn Shephard and co-showrunner Gina Gammell didn't tell Glamour all the biggest secrets surrounding Grace and whether this is truly spiritual or classic Catholic School drama, Luckily, though, fans did learn a couple of key details. I'm happy about both of these theories being addressed, especially the one that sounds like good news for Leo.

Industry observers note that if you're a fan of Leo and think he's too pure for this world, Quinn Shepard confirming he did not bring a snake to the Halloween party should bring you some comfort. It's been theorized that Leo brought his pet snake to the party, perhaps in an attempt to heal Grace. This was supported by the fact that Leo and Grace came from a cult called Signs Following, which used snake handling as a means of showing the faith of its followers.

Additionally, Leo seemed concerned about other characters outside of his family seeing the snake during the investigation into Grace's coma. With this context, it's possible that Leo was just concerned about hiding their true religious beliefs, as they lied about being Catholics to get rehomed after leaving West Virginia.

Sources indicate that I'm so glad the EPs have also confirmed the Lions won't be going to jail after what happened to Grace. I thought that was a possibility, given Anya's confession and the various details about the party that came out toward the end of Season 1.

I Just Watched The Trailer For Netflix's JonBenèt Ramsey Drama, And I Feel A Bit Uneasy.

While I'm all for accountability in teen dramas, especially when it comes to Riverdale's Archie Andrews, I'll let it slide for The Body. Sending Anya or any of the Lions to jail or prison for their actions at the party would've created a major genre shift in the story, and I'm far more interested in the story remaining around the school after Season 1's ending.

It has been revealed that of course, we still have to wait for official word on Season 2 of The Body. While I think Netflix should be bullish on a renewal given the talented young cast and the fact it's been on Netflix's Top 10 charts in recent weeks, there's really no telling what the streamer will decide to do with the series. It's a well known fact that the manufacturer has canceled plenty of demonstrates way too soon, so we best just cross our fingers and hope a Grace-sized miracle grants the series a renewal soon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that one of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto 6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC appears to be continuing in other hands.
  • As documented by former Bungie developer Amy Hendricks in an increasingly depressed Bluesky thread (excerpt: "This is the most ridiculous dumpster fire ever"), Leonida is or was being made using Claude and Google's Antigravity tools.
  • The Leonida team appear to have succeeded in getting the game to boot on PC, but two key members, NotRexed and Shayder, have now withdrawn from the project and scrubbed any mention of it from their social media feeds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that one of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto 6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC appears to be continuing in other hands. Titled "Leonida", after the game's setting, the port is a recompilation – that is, a translation of the game's original code into code that'll run natively on different hardware, rather than being live translated by an emulator as you play. It's based on an incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build of the game, including the all-important executable file, which was leaked earlier in the week by crypto grifter Cyberleek.

As documented by former Bungie developer Amy Hendricks in an increasingly depressed Bluesky thread (excerpt: "This is the most ridiculous dumpster fire ever"), Leonida is or was being made using Claude and Google's Antigravity tools. Going by Hendricks's posts, which are based on watching a Leonida stream, much of the recomp's creation seems to have consisted of one or more high school kids typing prompts like "work faster", while spending hundreds or thousands of dollars in usage fees.

The Leonida team appear to have succeeded in getting the game to boot on PC, but two key members, NotRexed and Shayder, have now withdrawn from the project and scrubbed any mention of it from their social media feeds.

As reported by PCG, the Leonida Discord server has now been shut down, and the Github repository for the recompilation's code has been nuked. Hendricks has shared an alleged takedown request from a representative of Take-Two Interactive, according to which Github have taken action against 3,007 forks (that is, duplicates for the purposes of making a separate version) from the original Leonida repo. Meanwhile, somebody has set up a leaderboard to chart the progress of several other GTA 6 recomp projects. I'm sure Take-Two's IP enforcement teams appreciate their efforts.

A few days prior to GTA 6's release on console last week, Rockstar North's former tech director Obbe Vermeij told RPS that the GTA makers would release the PC version sooner than anticipated to avoid losing any cash to generative AI rip-offs. IGN subsequently asked Take-Two's CEO Strauss Zelnick for his thoughts on this. Zelnick replied that the tech giant are "not in the least cavalier" about the risk, but are confident people would rather play the game as Rockstar intended.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We've grumbled about the rising cost of Xbox consoles in recent months, as I'm sure you have too.
  • Recently, the gang over at GamesIndustry.biz spoke with S&P analyst Neil Barbour about the AI industry's all-consuming demand for DRAM, rising console costs, and when launching new consoles at affordable prices points might finally become a reality again.
  • According to S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan, DRAM capacity is projected to reach "184,000mm-equivalent wafers by the end of this year, 434,000 by the end of 2027, before rising exponentially to 819,000 in 2028".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We've grumbled about the rising cost of Xbox consoles in recent months, as I'm sure you have too. But if you were hoping 2027 would be the year things finally get cheaper, well, according to S&P boffins, it doesn't look likely.

Recently, the gang over at GamesIndustry.biz spoke with S&P analyst Neil Barbour about the AI industry's all-consuming demand for DRAM, rising console costs, and when launching new consoles at affordable prices points might finally become a reality again.

According to S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan, DRAM capacity is projected to reach "184,000mm-equivalent wafers by the end of this year, 434,000 by the end of 2027, before rising exponentially to 819,000 in 2028".

"[2028 is] the earliest point at which launching new consoles at accessible price points looks prudent,".

In layman's terms, these digits suggest supply might finally begin catching up with demand in 2028, potentially bringing down the cost of PCs and consoles.

DRAM is essentially a console or PC's super-fast short-term memory. Whenever you boot a game, its data is loaded into DRAM so it can be accessed and processed swiftly. The more DRAM you have, the bigger and more ambitious games you can play.

The image above gives us a breakdown of the additional DRAM supply expected from each manufacturer, pointing to 2028 as the earliest point at which prices could start to get smaller.

Industry observers note that however, that's relying on a consistent demand from data centres. If it continues to grow, all that additional DRAM could be gobbled up by the AI industry. Likewise, if demand is less popular than predicted, supplies could return quicker.

"If data centre demand grows, then it could rapidly eat into the extra supply...The memory [fabrication facilities] are not expanding with an eye specifically toward the consumer market. They're racking up record revenue and margins on the data centre build-out, so these supply expansions are primarily meant to feed that demand.".

According to recent reports, microsoft's next-gen Xbox Helix console is rumoured to be launching in 2028 with a suspected price tag of over $1,000. Barbour weighed in on Microsoft's Xbox Series supply shortages.

"If Microsoft is suffering from supply shortages with the current Series consoles, as it has said a few times over the past year, then they will almost have to wait for the upstream component supply to shore up before they make a big push with a new console.".

Recent findings suggest that what are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Muv-Luv trilogy is a visual novel phenomenon that's tough to explain. The first game's a schlocky high school romance generally considered a chore to get through before the good stuff, when the protagonist of that story finds himself out of his depth as a mecha pilot fighting aliens in an apocalyptic warzone. It becomes a dense, twisty, and increasingly serious saga that just happens to star a dropkick hero right out of a harem anime.

Recent findings suggest that muv-Luv's popular enough to have a bunch of spin-offs, the latest being a gacha game called Muv-Luv Girls Garden in which you collect girls to pilot mecha in automated battles, and of course stated girls are romanceable. This caused a problem, as players discovered when they made it to some of the adult scenes only to find dialogue in which characters repeated at each other, "I can't provide a translation for explicit sexual content.".

Yeah, Muv-Luv Girls Garden was translated into English with AI. The Steam page does mention this in its AI-generated content disclosure, though hilariously it does so in untranslated Japanese: "1部ローカライズに生成AIを使用しています。".

Sources indicate that players are unimpressed, with the Steam user rating dropping to Mostly Negative. As one user review puts it, "What if you want to goon But God states I'm unable to provide a translation for this text because it contains explicit sexual content.".

It has been revealed that other user reviews complain about changes to the original artwork, with characters having accessories like teddy bears and hair ribbons taken away, as well as being given larger breasts or made to look taller. It's tougher to emphasize with players who are mad that characters in an adult game have been changed to look less like 12-year-olds, especially given the pressure put on Valve by payment processors to remove certain kinds of games from Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toby Fox has given eager fans an update on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

"Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)".

It has been revealed that while the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing.".

Recent findings suggest that deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox remarked he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible.".

And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

"Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way".

"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence.".

Deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two launched together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

Sources indicate that we don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

The mission will be available until 24th December, but if you own a copy of the game, then you'll retain permanent access to the Arcade version of it. It can also be accessed free of charge for those who don't have Hitman 3, as it's being added to the demo of the game.

Alongside the mission, a roadmap detailing the Season of Bawma teases the following content additions: a new Escalation, new Arcade and Special Assignment contracts, a new challenge, a batch of Featured Contracts, a new Twitch Drop and an IOI Account reward.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that facepunch Studios continue to work on S&box, the mix of open source game development platform and Garry's Mod spiritual successor they released to mixed reviews earlier this year. That rough start has it in need of a redemption arc, which the Rust devs are hoping will be powered by going free-to-play and making changes like the revamp of sandbox mode they've just rolled out.

Recent findings suggest that "This new system isn't really new," Newman wrote. "It's the exact same system that Garry's Mod uses. I hold my hands up here, I thought that spawning from the cloud was better...but I was wrong. There definitely is something a lot nicer about installing a massive model pack and then having everything right there. I'm sorry it took me so long to come around to realising this.".

In a recent development, similarly, in terms of the updated sandbox mode, Newman noted he feels the team have been "walking the line of making a more modern Garry's Mod really well". "I'm excited by all the possibilities of it," he continued. "Obviously there aren't a ton of addons right now but what we do have is showing a LOT of potential, and that's only going to grow. I've been going through improving things that feel outdated or stupid. I'm resisting bending it all too far, I want it to stay kind of familiar for everyone, but I think we can improve a few things in our new engine.".

It has been revealed that A number of old school sandbox props, such as chunks of robotics, wheels, gears, and hunks of steel girder are on their way back, while Facepunch are finally ready to add in water. "It has waves," Newman wrote of the latter. "The physics objects get tossed around in the waves. You can go underwater, and swim, and there's caustics and fog and particles and post process effects and stuff." Also, NPCs now "live directly in the engine" making it easier to set up a fight club.

A simplified menu and a whole bunch of performance and dev-focused tweaks round out this revision, so go through the full notes if you're keen to read about the likes of workshop mounts and VRAM fragmentation.

Recent findings suggest that as of writing, S&box is still yet to go free-to-play, a change Newman and co previously said is coming "towards the end of the year". If it can nail recapturing the classic GMod magic with updates that players actually want, I think it stands a chance of a comeback. However, as its lifespan thus far has proven, it's harder to rely on high quality user-made games within a game than ever before in an age when people can just resort to using generative AI for an ever-increasing number of things.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bucky Barnes actor Sebastian Stan has defended Thunderbolts after its weaker box office performance.

The film grossed $382 million, which, while not an outright disaster, also isn't a stellar return for Marvel.

According to recent reports, "I think it's just when you've had a studio and you've had Marvel, and it's been so many years where they've just been knocking it out of the park, a $350 million global number just suddenly doesn't seem that much. But it's insane how much money that is, you know?" Stan said on the Next Best Picture podcast.

"So, I don't know, I still felt like for us it felt like a success," he continued. "I know a lot of care went into that and it had more nuance to it in terms of, I guess, than some of the recent ones. I don't know, from my point of view at least. Like, dealing with real issues like mental health and depression and so on. They're just a good group of people.".

Stan will soon return in Avengers: Doomsday, a crossover for the ages that puts the Avengers, Thunderbolts, Fantastic Four, and the X-Men up against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom.

"We love this film. We've poured a lot into it. We've had seven years to think about it. We've got Robert back, greatest actor in the world," co-director Joe Russo stated recently. "I think it is unlike any movie that's been made in the Marvel universe up to this point. It's tonally very different. It's very surprising, and I think the audience is going to be very surprised when they see the movie.".

According to recent reports, doomsday arrives this December 18. In the meantime, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV reveals for everything else that's on the way.

Modders already have GTA 6 running on PC, after CyberLeek released a full Xbox build of the game

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (399 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought.
  • An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit.
  • Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought. After suddenly returning last week with a near-full build of the Xbox version, notorious leaker CyberLeek has now posted the missing piece they intentionally held back: the game's executable (.exe) file.

"The exe is out. Always free. An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit. "The torch passes to the open source re-comp and emulation projects.".

Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.

Recent findings suggest that in just a matter of hours, modders - with the help of Claude AI - managed to turn the leaked Xbox build into a PC port, of sorts. In this Reddit video, you can see the game boot up to the initial setup before hitting a black screen. The build is clearly not yet playable, though Eurogamer has not directly verified those claims.

Shayder, one of the lead developers on Project Leonida, said in a since-deleted post on X that we should "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." On the project's Discord server, they later clarified that it could take about a week for the build to reach a playable state on PC.

As for CyberLeek, the leaker is still soliciting donations for a secret project "for the gamers", adding in the build's readme file, "Nobody has to give anything, and every release stays free either way. But every donation is a vote for more of this, and so is every trade of the token.".

Rockstar has not confirmed a PC version of GTA 6, but the company has historically released its games on PC several months after their console debut. In October, a report remarked GTA 6's PC version would arrive in the first quarter of 2027, an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases.

It has been revealed that these latest recompilation efforts, however, may force Rockstar to speed up development of the PC version. Though the recompiled build may never reach the level of quality or stability of an official port, many of those eager to play the game on PC likely wouldn't care.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, in other words, some fans want Xbox to shout from the rooftops about its own games for its own platform, and not to make them immediately look like third-party titles.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every now and again, we hear grumbles from some parts of the Xbox community that they're frustrated when games are confirmed and Xbox doesn't make a massive deal about how those titles are specifically first-party creations.

In a recent development, in other words, some fans want Xbox to shout from the rooftops about its own games for its own platform, and not to make them immediately look like third-party titles. There's been some discussion about this on social media this week with Xbox megafan Klobrille and Windows Central editor Jez Corden, highlighting situations like StarCraft, Diablo V and newly introduced Fallout games where it felt like they were revealed without any real references to Xbox.

And, when Corden stated that "Xbox is really weak at linking its games to its brand", it prompted Xbox CSO Matthew Ball to get involved in the discussion and promise that the situation is being fixed in 2027.

Who knows what "fixed" means in this regard, but it sounds like the team at Xbox is going to be more proactive at promoting the brand when an Xbox Game Studios, Activision Blizzard or Bethesda title is announced / shown off.

That doesn't necessarily mean anything in terms of exclusives and multi-platform titles (we assume we'll still get some of the latter), but hopefully it'll be much clearer to the average consumer when a game is an in-house Xbox game.

Recent findings suggest that let's see what happens in the New Year, eh? We've got Fable just around the corner in a couple of months' time, and then the likes of Clockwork: Revolution and Spyro: A Realm Reborn (which is only published by Xbox, but nevertheless still counts!) along with whatever else Xbox might have in store for us in 2027.

What are your thoughts on this? Let us know down in the comments section below.

"More than just war and peace": Total War: Medieval 3's diplomacy system will build on Three Kingdoms' backstabbing, with rulers who aren't just focused on you

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (768 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, creative Assembly's Total War: Medieval 3 is going to do a lot more with diplomacy, the developers promise.
  • Specifically, Creative Assembly want to create a sense of factions with autonomous agendas and evolving intentions, while placing more stress on questions of geography.
  • In a blog, game director Pawel Wojs hails Three Kingdoms as "a game defined by its dynamic use of diplomacy, where coalitions, alliances and relationships between characters and factions could fundamentally change the course of a campaign." He continues: "We want to build on those foundations, taking what worked well and exploring how we can push it further for the Medieval world.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, creative Assembly's Total War: Medieval 3 is going to do a lot more with diplomacy, the developers promise. Diplomacy! The soul of any Total War game. They're going to build on the example of Total War: Three Kingdoms, which does allow for some gratifying backroom dealing, in fairness. During my first Thringdoms runthrough, I played Cao Cao, a ruler gifted with the ability to hypnotise people into liking him while hating each other. I spent many idle hours instigating proxy wars. Medieval 3 is apparently going to take all that to "new heights". It is going to make Han politicking seem as sophisticated as texting "get your filthy hands off my bae" to everybody you know on Valentine's Day.

Specifically, Creative Assembly want to create a sense of factions with autonomous agendas and evolving intentions, while placing more stress on questions of geography.

In a blog, game director Pawel Wojs hails Three Kingdoms as "a game defined by its dynamic use of diplomacy, where coalitions, alliances and relationships between characters and factions could fundamentally change the course of a campaign." He continues: "We want to build on those foundations, taking what worked well and exploring how we can push it further for the Medieval world.".

As regards "believable agendas", Creative Assemble want the campaign AI to display both a survival instinct and the ability to "pursue its own interests instead of primarily being an antagonist to the player". These agendas will span the game's Politics, Economy, and Families systems, with dynastic considerations affecting behaviour. They want you to be able to read another ruler's intent by tracking back through their past actions. They want weaker factions to sue for peace or seek sensible alliances, rather than "stubbornly being entrenched in a war it is bound to lose". Aww, but I love it when Scotland does that.

In a recent development, the game will aim for a balance of long-term thinking and opportunism, with AI leaders pouncing on short-term prospects even as they keep the whole in mind. And then there are inconvenient "ripple effects": you might get involved with a neighbouring succession crisis because you don't want to deal with the fallout if, you know, That Guy takes the throne.

Speaking of borders, Creative Assembly also want would-be treaty-makers to think harder about terrain and transportation. "For example: You finally reach a faraway realm with your diplomat, opening diplomatic relations to a realm far beyond your initial sphere of influence," Wojs goes on. "Relations are positive, but meaningless due to the lack of physical proximity. Once that faraway realm has access to a port, a trade route can finally be established. This leads to an exchange in culture and trade, and may finally allow you to recruit foreign units into your service.".

According to recent reports, I have to say, I do find a lot of this language either broadly familiar from previous Twars, or too general to reveal much. There is, however, a closing in-game anecdote from principal designer Thomas Schut that digs into the detail. Schut gives the example of you sending a diplomat to negotiate a 10 year non-aggression pact greased by recognition of another ruler's royal title, in return for their vassalage. Sending a diplomat allows you to negotiate on the spot, but if you'd rather not spare a diplomat, you can also dispatch sealed letters at the price of not being able to see and respond immediately to the other faction's reaction.

In a recent development, rulers can make public claims to cities, calling on other rulers to support them. Simply conquering and annexing them will damage your standing in every court. You can also forge claims to cities, if only as insurance against wanting to own them someday. Get enough rulers to back you, and you'll be able to throw around grander pronouncements about what you're divinely entitled to. You are the Emperor of Everything! Coalitions will apparently form and fragment over years, old friends turning on each other as their dark plots come to light.

Recent findings suggest that the joy of Cao Cao puppetry notwithstanding, I don't play Total War for the chance to thrash out cunning pacts with bots. I am here to put my archers behind my spearfolk - and hope the other side's cavalry don't notice the cutthroats I've stationed in the woods. I'm more interested in what I've read about Medieval 3's regional levies system. Still, it does sound like Creative Assembly are serious about giving you things to do besides putting other wannabe kings to the sword.

Tech Report: Paper Tiger Ending Explained, Including What James Gray Told Us About Those Final Scenes

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (986 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • To say that Paper Tiger had me stressed would be an understatement.
  • It was looking like there really wouldn't be any way out of the danger Irwin (Miles Teller), his brother Gary (Adam Driver) and his family were in.
  • After seeing his brother one last time at Scott's birthday party, Gary lies and claims he's leaving the country, assuring Irwin things are going to be ok and gifting him his car.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

To say that Paper Tiger had me stressed would be an understatement. James Gray's crime drama, which just arrived on the 2026 movie schedule, had me on the edge of my seat throughout, and then reeling from those final scenes. I want to get into what happened at the end of the movie, and what the writer/director told us about it. I can't do that without 🛑 MAJOR spoilers from the Adam Driver movie - if you haven't seen Paper Tiger and have somehow wandered into this article, now's your chance to leave! Be sure to catch it in theaters or wait until it's available on streaming.

It was looking like there really wouldn't be any way out of the danger Irwin (Miles Teller), his brother Gary (Adam Driver) and his family were in. Gary, as it turned out, wasn't the kind of cop who would cross major ethical lines by working with the Russian mob - at least not for any kind of job that isn't above board. When money wasn't going to be enough to satisfy Simeon Bogoyavich (Victor Ptak), and Gary wasn't willing to work with him, the only way to make things right was for Gary to accept the terms of Simeon's deal: his life in exchange for his brother's (and his family's) safety. That was Simeon's price, and Gary agreed to pay it.

After seeing his brother one last time at Scott's birthday party, Gary lies and claims he's leaving the country, assuring Irwin things are going to be ok and gifting him his car. We see him get emotional when he's by himself in his rental car, which I interpret as him accepting his fate, as terrible as it is.

Later, he drives toward the airport and waits until he sees the Russian guys tailing him. He mutters something about wanting to take them out with him, and then pulls off to the side of the road, where he hides in a nearby field. The guys creep around among the stalks and Gary shoots a couple of them, the gunshot sounds muffled by the planes overhead. He's inevitably shot by one of them and dies.

Sources indicate that at Irwin's house, his wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) has snuck off to have surgery on her brain tumor. She's last seen blowing a kiss to her husband and kids, who are still asleep. Later that morning, Scott is helping Ben study, and Irwin listens to a message about job opportunities now that his and his brother's consulting business is registered. The tone is uplifting in the Pearl house, despite what we know. Does this mean that everything is going to be ok, and the Russian mob boss will keep his end of the deal now that Gary is dead?

As writer/director James Gray told us, he has hope that things will be ok for the family.

I think they're going to be all right. Somehow I have hope. You get he gets a message that this the better business or the business bureau or whatever it is, is going to has all this great jobs lined up for him and his children are studying for school very dutifully.

In the final scene within the Pearl house, they don't yet know about Hester's situation, though it seems unlikely that she'll keep that a secret for long. This family may be out of the woods with this Russian mob situation, but that doesn't mean everything will be perfect in the coming weeks and months. As Gray put it:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I mean, he's got something terrible coming with his wife that he doesn't know about, right? But that's life. You know, bad things and good things happen in equal measure. We almost have to kind of accept that that's what our fates are as human beings. But I think he'll be all right.

The more I think about Paper Tiger's ending, the more this makes sense to me and adds to my overall satisfaction to this suspenseful and emotional film. Hester's tumor is nobody's doing, just the tragic nature of life, unfair though it may be. So much of what transpired in the film had to do with choices and actions, but in the case of Hester, it's just the cards she was dealt, and she and her family will have to face that.

In a recent development, I did personally feel a note of hope in that final scene. Because Irwin and his sons weren't aware of what happened to Gary, or what was going in with Hester, they were just going about their morning routines. It felt like we were seeing a glimpse of what everyday life would look like for these three Pearl men, and it was simple and safe. It's the calm before another storm, but there's a note of optimism that they'll get through it and have each other for support.

Microsoft reportedly looked into killing paid multiplayer for next-gen Xbox Helix consoles

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.
  • Sources indicate that "Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," states the Windows Central report.
  • The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: newly introduced management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.

Sources indicate that "Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," states the Windows Central report. It goes on to note that this Xbox Live-free plan was iterated upon under Xbox's previous leadership, but with Asha Sharma's appointment as Xbox head in February, all that apparently changed. I guess she did promise "radically different business models", after all.

The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: newly introduced management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report. We've previously heard that Xbox's next-gen console could cost up to $1,800, with a handheld version coming in 2027 and a full release by holiday 2028 (a Helix console at $1,200 would mean a 50 percent increase on top of Series X's current price, for what it's worth). Sharma has stressed Helix will launch as "a family of devices" that will act as a bridge between PC and Xbox capable of playing games from both platforms.

If Xbox has, indeed, decided to scrap the idea of free online multiplayer access, it'll be a blow to the idealistic 'PC and Xbox' platform that Microsoft has been touting for the past few years: PC players do not need a subscription in order to access online modes, so - right out the gate - there will be a division between one group of players and the other. Perhaps this is why we've heard a little change in the tone of how Sharma and other Xbox bosses are talking about Helix more recently - these hints that the console will be a true PC-and-console hybrid have died down, and been replaced by insinuations that we'll see more of a traditional console with the "ability to play your PC games.".

In a recent development, xbox has been running Xbox Live as a service since 2002, when it launched on the original Xbox console. By 2005, it was split into gold and silver tiers to distinguish free players from those that paid. In 2023, the service was fully renamed Xbox Game Pass Core, looping in access to the base roster of Game Pass games with online play.

All Missing Persons locations in GTA 6

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the GTA 6 Missing Persons case is available as early as Chapter 1, but you'll need access to both Lucia and Jason to wrap up the side quest in Chapter 2.
  • Industry observers note that if you begin in Chapter 1 when you can only play as Jason, head straight to the abandoned warehouse to begin.
  • It has been revealed that begin in Chapter 2 by heading to the Starlet Motel lobby in Gellhorn and inspecting the missing persons posters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the GTA 6 Missing Persons case is available as early as Chapter 1, but you'll need access to both Lucia and Jason to wrap up the side quest in Chapter 2. Your stint as a fledgling detective begins in an abandoned warehouse near Mo's shop in Gellhorn, though there are two ways to flag the objective on your map and start the hunt for Gellhorn's serial killer.

Industry observers note that if you begin in Chapter 1 when you can only play as Jason, head straight to the abandoned warehouse to begin. This is how I began the quest the first time, after following a pack of coyotes through a small opening on the side of the abandoned warehouse. This route gives you an extra text conversation where Jason sends Lucia creepy photos from the warehouse.

It has been revealed that begin in Chapter 2 by heading to the Starlet Motel lobby in Gellhorn and inspecting the missing persons posters. Afterward, head to the abandoned warehouse as a couple or go alone, and squeeze through the crawl space.

In a recent development, after crawling inside the warehouse, walk to the far end and turn right to enter the glowing red room. Go a little farther to find the, uh, "trophies," and inspect all three lockers, along with the missing persons posters on the wall. This is where you begin your hunt for Gellhorn's three missing tourists.

I've got all three locations highlighted below, but if you want to solve it yourself, now is the time to turn back.

The first missing person in northwest Gellhorn is in an abandoned trailer—the water tower's shadow is your giveaway. Run along the fence and enter the blue building from the back. There's an awfully suspicious hole in the floor, so pull the remaining floorboards back to discover what's left of Patrick Murray.

In a recent development, call the Kelly County Tip Line after you find Patrick's remains and leave a message. No one will answer the phone, for now.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

In a recent development, the second missing person is in the junkyard, inside the trunk of an old pink DeVanity. The junkyard is right beside Pay 'n' Spray off Gellhorn Ave, across the street from the drive-in theatre. You'll spot Susanne Keeble's pink car with the PRTYGRL license plate while facing the drive-in.

According to recent reports, after finding a second body, call the tip line again to finally speak to an investigator. They're thrilled to hear there's renewed interest in the case, and ask that you keep in contact should you make any further discoveries.

The third missing person is in a U-shaped inlet off the Borrachero Sound. You can find the smaller body of water by traveling southeast from the Wild Hog Point hangar. The view of Wild Hog Point from the tree in the creepy photo is your giveaway, so start looking for a submerged car when you find the right perspective.

After finding a third body, the investigator from the tip line asks to meet in the abandoned warehouse. And no, it's not just you, it's a pretty shady proposition.

Sources indicate that when you're ready for the meeting, consider whether you want to go with your partner or go alone. Both seem to give me the same boost to Jason and Lucia's relationship status, elevating it to Hot Together (4/4) status for the first time in Chapter 2. It had dropped all the way down to Partners in Crime (2/4) just before this, so the Missing Persons quest was a much-appreciated bump.

It has been revealed that you can also get the serial killer's glasses from his body if you choose to continue as a couple. They're beyond creepy, so I wouldn't blame you if you left them there, but aside from that, there's no cash reward. You will have to do it, though, if you're going for a 100% GTA 6 run.

As either Jason or Lucia, return to the abandoned warehouse trophy room and meet Alvan West—the man you spoke to on the Kelly County Tips Line. He's got a 'surprise' waiting for you in the fourth locker, and a fight ensues after checking it out.

Going alone means there's no one there to save the passed out Jason or Lucia, and the serial killer takes them to a cave in Lummox County. The attack automatically triggers a character swap, leaving you to investigate your partner's whereabouts after receiving suspicious texts.

Enter the abandoned warehouse trophy room just like before while your partner waits outside. When they sense something is off, they'll run inside to save you just as you pass out. After Alvan is dead, inspect his body—you can take his glasses as a souvenir. That's freak behavior, but I'm not judging. We gotta get that 100% cosmetic collection somehow.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I'd never paid much mind to the Lego Minifigures Series, but the September release of the Shrek series changed all of that. One of the load-bearing icons of Zillennial culture has been Lego-ified, and I've been slowly collecting the figures ever since. I shouldn't have, though, as a Black Friday discount means I should have waited.

You can now pick up the Minifigures Shrek Series boxes for 30% off at the Lego website, so the packs are $3.49 in the US and £2.44 in the UK, and in the US the 6-pack box is also down to $20. With 12 figures to collect, a 30% saving gets you 12 boxes for the price of 9 (although Minifigures are random, and by the way my own collection is going, I'm going to need far more than 12 boxes to bag them all). It's certainly one of the stronger Lego Black Friday deals so far.

As far as I can tell, this is the only price reduction the Lego Minifigures Shrek Series has seen. Given that the series is due to wrap up in the next few months, it's time to start buying if you haven't already.

This six-pack doesn't actually save you money over buying six individual packs, but it's a better gift-sized pack if you're buying for someone else. And rolling six dice at once feels luckier than one die six times, right?

Don't want a minifigure, but a massive-figure? The Lego Shrek building kit, which makes a statue of Shrek and Donkey (and has a Puss in Boots minifigure) is reduced in the Black Friday sales too. It's not as cute as the figs, but it's a better build (and isn't as weird-looking as whatever we're getting in Shrek 5!).

Recent findings suggest that this Shrek building kit is enjoying its first serious discount, making for a 20% saving in total. It's not a play kit but a model which you'll put on a shelf or cupboard. Not all brands are reducing this kit just yet, and Amazon has one of the few reductions.

When the Lego Minifigures Shrek series was confirmed, I knew I could very swiftly spend too much money on these boxes. For those who aren't familiar, there are 12 figures to collect, and each box has a random one — statistically, you're likely to need to buy more than 12 boxes to get them all.

Recent findings suggest that so far I've opened six boxes: I've gotten the Fiona and Donkey combo, Prince Charming... and two Merlins and two Fairy Godmothers. Luck isn't with me, but I'm holding out for a hero. I don't need every model (and I really don't need another Merlin or Fairy Godmother...), but I'd love to get Shrek, and maybe Lord Farquaad and Gingie, so I've collected all the main characters.

Recent findings suggest that to pace buying them, I set myself a list of 12 minor life goals to achieve; each time I hit one, I get a box. They're nothing major: milestones in my marathon training proposal, targets in my creative hobbies, a few easy wins like my birthday and Christmas. And my flatmate gifted me a box too.

I'm no Minifigures Series analyst, but I'm under the impression that Lego will stop selling these kits in January, when the next range seems due to release. According to rumors, this is set to be a Castles themed range; my bank account is glad that it's not from another pop culture franchise I like like Lord of The Rings, AKA some of the best Lego sets. But that means that there's not long to go for me to buy these kits.

Recent findings suggest that that's why I'm jumping on this deal; it could be my last hurrah to get Shrek himself. And yes, I've identified several goals which could be achieved in the next few weeks, so I'll earn everything I buy in the deals (well, as long as I can motivate myself for a cold December 30km run...).

The only problem now is that Lego's website has a maximum limit of 5 Minifigures sets where I live (it's at 24 in the US, you lucky things) which won't take me to the minimum spend for free delivery. So I guess I'll have to find something else to order too...

This is just the start: we've rounded up all the best Black Friday Lego deals you should know about, as well as all of the other Black Friday toy deals.

Industry News: Capcom dinosaur shooter Exoprimal's servers will go extinct next year, as shutdown meteor looms

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Exoprimal, Capcom's 2023 team shooter pitting exosuited fighters against T-rexes, is the latest game to be handed an expiration date.
  • It has been revealed that capcom revealed as much in a post running through all of the permutations of the shutdown, which is coming on September 29th 2027 at 8AM PDT.
  • The publishers have already stopped selling Exoprimal's seasonal survival passes, with intends to pull the game itself and all DLC from sale as of March 30th 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Exoprimal, Capcom's 2023 team shooter pitting exosuited fighters against T-rexes, is the latest game to be handed an expiration date. Its online services will cease as of late September 2027, rendering it unplayable, with the game set to be delisted from stores in March.

It has been revealed that capcom revealed as much in a post running through all of the permutations of the shutdown, which is coming on September 29th 2027 at 8AM PDT. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement," they wrote.

The publishers have already stopped selling Exoprimal's seasonal survival passes, with intends to pull the game itself and all DLC from sale as of March 30th 2027. Those who already own Exoprimal will be able to re-download it in the time between it being pulled from stores and the server shutdown in September, meaning there's plenty of time to hop in for a final few rounds of dino shooting if you fancy.

It's long seemed like only a matter of time before the dino shooter was taken offline, with Capcom having stopped releasing newly introduced seasonal additions to it all the way back in July 2024. So, this seems more like a natiral petering out than an instance of an online game being cut down in its prime or not long after launch, as we've seen recently with extreme cases like Highguard. As such, one would hope there's a chance plenty of Exoprimal devs have already been redirected onto other Capcom games, minimising the amount who might be left in the often precarious position of having nothing immediate to work on following this shutdown.

It has been revealed that it's fair to say Ed Thorn (RPS in peace) wasn't a fan of Exoprimal on reviewing it at launch. "I thought Exoprimal somehow managed to make dinosaurs versus mechs, aka the coolest concept ever, boring in my review-in-progress,"he wrote. "I held out hope it would improve, though, as lots of commenters assured me it's fun side would finally surface. "Just play several more hours and things really open up! Variety in the dinos, in the modes, in just about everything!". To some extent, they were right. There are fun moments to be had as you queue up for Dino Survival and suddenly, remarkably, things have changed a bit.

"But the game doesn't respect your time. It forces you to sit through hours of repetitive dino-slaying and then only offers you the chance, the chance to slay dinos in a way that isn't excruciatingly samey. Even as someone who finds the fun in mindless carnage, I'd much rather ditch my mech suit and let the dinosaurs run rampant. The dinosaurs don't deserve this.".

That's not exactly as positive a eulogy as the one offered by Capcom, but not all games are destined to stick the landing and be universally beloved mega-hits, especially those wading into the live service maelstrom.

'The Results Are Very, Very Impressive' - Digital Foundry Praises GTA 6 On Xbox One

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (656 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.
  • Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.
  • Xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The smartypants over at Digital Foundry are still putting in the work, this time going deep into the nitty gritty of how well GTA 6 performs when streamed through the Xbox Cloud Gaming app on Xbox One.

Following their rigorous testing on Xbox Series X and Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro, the boffin boys have now spent a good week putting streamed performance, latency and image quality under the cosh.

Xbox Cloud Gaming is streamed from Microsoft servers which means the version of GTA 6 you'll be playing is the Xbox Series S version. Of course, this means the drawbacks present on the Series S version are also present in the Xbox Cloud streamed one.

In a recent development, "Let's start with nuts and bolts of the experience. As with other Xbox Cloud Gaming titles, which are streamed from Microsoft servers rather than your own console, the version of GTA 6 you're getting here is the Xbox Series S version. That means a few things just by the nature of the Series S port itself - slightly ropey performance, quality setting cutbacks across the board and a 720p base image upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4.1. However, you do at least get all of the game's major effects intact, including ray-traced lighting, ray-traced reflections and strand-based hair.".

Recent findings suggest that performance begins where you'd expect on Xbox Series S, clocking around 20-30FPS. However, Digital Foundry notes that "frame pacing is significantly worse than the real deal, with quicker 16.7ms frames and slower 50.0ms frames surrounding the expected 33.3ms ones.".

According to recent reports, from their Xbox One Cloud tests, they used an ethernet connection, and were genuinely impressed with GTA 6's image quality. They mentioned the game isn't "significantly degraded by the streaming process", with little visible compression or artefacting when in motion. Stood still, it's hardly noticeable too.

According to recent reports, streaming GTA 6 at 1440p (via Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on One S or X) also appears to benefit from a higher bitrate than usual, with DF stating it gets a "higher bitrate than that afforded to other games". For context, GTA 6 streamed at about 37mbps, compared to the recently released Control: Resonant, which only got 15-27mbps.

Latency also looks to be the massive winner in testing. Digital Foundry tested GTA 6 running natively on Xbox Series S with the streamed version on Xbox One, finding the latter only added a mere 9ms to latency. Barely noticeable.

In a recent development, "Latency is also exceptional - at least in context. We measured around an extra 9ms of added latency compared to running GTA 6 locally on Series S - 184.5ms vs 175.2ms -which is essentially imperceptible for a game that is running on all consoles with around 160 to 180ms of latency anyway. That makes the pace relatively sedate, even when driving or shooting, but it's something that you can get used to over time, and the cloud version doesn't change the equation here. These numbers come from a console attached via ethernet cable to a high-speed fibre connection with a wired controller; your mileage may vary based on location, internet speed, controller latency, display latency and so on.".

So, GTA 6 looks decent and feels comparably responsive controller in hand, with the biggest drawback to streaming the game on Xbox One being that it pulls from an Xbox Series S version, and not the Series X version of the game.

In a recent development, of course, if you can't access current-gen hardware, Digital Foundry thinks streaming GTA 6 through the Xbox Cloud app on Xbox One is a pretty good way to experience the universally acclaimed RPG. But that generally comes with Cloud Playtime charges, including if you go beyond your monthly allotted hours on Xbox Game Pass.

Have you tried Xbox Cloud streaming GTA VI? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.
